title: CMSIS Debugger: Attach to a core without program image is refused
cause: The Disassembly view opens only for the selected core; opening it for a second, attached core from the CALL STACK context menu failed (a UX problem).
fix: Select the second core in the CALL STACK view first, then open the Disassembly view; the multi-core debug section of the CMSIS Debugger README describes this.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Live View only updates when the target is stopped (ST-Link)
cause: A faulty "true" value of the auxiliaryGdb setting in the launch configuration; the thread does not say what exactly was wrong with it.
fix: Check the auxiliaryGdb entry in the launch configuration; once it was corrected, Live View also updated while running with ST-Link. The thread does not give the corrected value.

message: E: bad pack name: it should be one of the following formats: Vendor.Pack, Vendor.Pack.x.y.z, Vendor.Pack.x.y.z.pack, or Vendor.Pack.pdsc
title: cpackget: cpackget rejects pack names that start with a digit
cause: The name pattern of cpackget 0.9.0 ([a-zA-Z][0-9a-zA-Z_\-]+) required a letter as first character, whereas the pack schema allows digits, underscores and dashes in any position ([-_A-Za-z0-9]+).
fix: No fix in the thread; the maintainer planned to adapt cpackget to the pack schema's name pattern.

message:
*** ERROR M310: <pack>.pdsc (Line 465)
  Filename mismatch (case sensitive):
title: packchk: ERROR M310 Filename mismatch for an example doc attribute with ../ segments
cause: packchk did not resolve the ../ segments of the example's doc attribute relative to the example folder before comparing the names.
fix: The thread gives no confirmed fix.

message:
*** WARNING M300: <pack>.pdsc (Line 776) 
  at must use 'https://'
title: packchk: packchk 2.9.0 warns M300 for XML namespace URLs that start with http
cause: The https check of packchk 2.9.0 (an attribute loop introduced in #1109) also flags xmlns namespace declarations of extension elements. A namespace URL is only an identifier and cannot be changed without breaking its consumers; only schemaLocation should need https.
fix: No fix in the thread. A schemaLocation should use https; the warning on the namespace URL itself cannot be removed from the pdsc.

title: pyOCD: mbed LPC1768 not found by pyocd on Windows 10 although mbed-ls lists it
cause: The mbed LPC1768 interface firmware (rev 141212) exposes only the USB mass-storage interface under Windows 10; the CMSIS-DAP HID interface never appears, so no debugger can see the probe and pyOCD cannot fix it.
fix: The thread gives no confirmed fix.

title: pyOCD: Chip erase on STM32WB55 fails: flash algorithm runs on the wrong core
cause: STM32WB is dual-core with shared flash, and its reference manual says a mass erase issued by CPU1 (the Cortex-M4) is ignored with a bus error. pyOCD always ran flash operations on the first core and ignored the Pname of the pack's algorithm element, although the maintainer noted the failure was reported by EraseChip() rather than as a bus error. A full chip erase with that pack also failed in Keil MDK.
fix: No fix in the thread; the maintainer said pyOCD would have to run the flash algorithm on the core named by the algorithm's Pname attribute.

message: 'JLinkProbe' object has no attribute '_lock'
title: pyOCD: J-Link session open fails with AttributeError: JLinkProbe has no attribute '_lock'
cause: Regression in 0.27: JLinkProbe lacks the _lock attribute that DebugProbe.lock() uses, so opening a session with a J-Link fails.
fix: The previous pyOCD version worked for the reporter; the maintainer said he would get a fix out soon.

message: 0000464:ERROR:__main__:uncaught exception: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'tuple' and 'int'
title: pyOCD: STM32F401RE pack fails: not enough space for flash algorithm, then TypeError
cause: The STM32F401RE has 128 kB sectors, so the flash algorithm and its data buffer do not fit in the available RAM; the pack sector parsing also mishandled the (start, size) tuples, causing the TypeError.
fix: No fix in the thread. Unpacking the tuple in cmsis_pack.py removes the TypeError, but the region then has no flash algorithm; the maintainer planned to support separate erase and program sizes for pack flash algorithms.

message: 0000861:WARNING:rom_table:Invalid coresight component, cidr=0x0
title: pyOCD: STM32H743 ROM table probe fails with memory transfer fault on connect
cause: The maintainer said this is the same as the STM32L4S5 case: STM32H7 and F7 parts need DBGMCU_CR set to wake the debug domain and keep it awake before CoreSight discovery, otherwise ROM table reads fault. This was not confirmed for this board.
fix: A pyocd_user.py that writes DBGMCU_CR (0xE00E1004 on H743) through raw AP0 CSW/TAR/DRW writes right after dp_init was suggested, also with value 0x00670007; neither worked for the reporter. pyOCD did connect after STM32CubeIDE had connected first, as long as --connect=under-reset was not used.

message: 0001982:INFO:loader:Erased 0 bytes (0 sectors), programmed 0 bytes (0 pages), skipped 0 bytes (0 pages) at 0.00 kB/s
title: pyOCD: pyocd flash reports 0 bytes programmed although erase works
cause: The maintainer suspected that the ELF has no programmable sections, for example because it is linked to run from RAM instead of flash; the thread does not confirm it.
fix: List the sections with arm-none-eabi-objdump -h <file>.elf to check their addresses and attributes, or try converting the ELF to a binary with arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary.

message: 0007677 E Error while running debug sequence 'ResetSystem' (core cm33_core0): Memory transfer fault [pack_target]
title: pyOCD: LPC55S69 flash download via GDB fails with memory transfer fault
cause: The flash download over GDB failed in the ResetSystem debug sequence run after loading; the maintainers linked it to the reset sequence problem of issue #92.
fix: Follow the resolution of issue #92 on the ResetSystem sequence; this thread only links to it.

message: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'name'
title: pyOCD: CMSIS-DAP connect raises AttributeError on a None protocol in v0.30
cause: A trace log statement in the CMSIS-DAP probe connect() accesses protocol.name while the protocol is None.
fix: The thread gives no confirmed fix.

message: CRITICAL:__main__:No cores were discovered!
title: pyOCD: STM32G0 (NUCLEO-G071RB): 'No cores were discovered!' with invalid CoreSight CIDR values
cause: The maintainer suspected, from the debug sequences of the STM32G0 pack, that RCC_APBENR1.DBGEN must be set to clock the debug resources before the ROM tables are read; flashing with STM32CubeIDE probably leaves it set, which would explain why the error disappears after flashing that way.
fix: Proposed, not confirmed: a pyocd_user.py whose will_init_target hook inserts a task after 'create_aps' that writes 0x08000000 to 0x4002103c. On pyOCD 0.21.0 the parameter had to be named init_sequence, and the script then still failed with a NoneType error.

message: DP IDCODE read failed; resending SWJ sequence (use dormant=False)
title: pyOCD: DAPLink probe: DP IDCODE read failed or No ACK, board not auto-detected
cause: Maintainers said 'No ACK' and 'DP IDCODE read failed' usually mean the probe cannot talk to the target, most often because the target is in a low-power mode. Board auto-detection needs a DAPLink build with a built-in target; standalone HIC builds report an all-zero board ID.
fix: Suggested, not confirmed: connect under reset (pyocd erase --connect=under-reset; the option is --connect, not --connect-mode), and check wiring, target power and the probe. For auto-detection use a DAPLink build made for the board.

message: ERROR:root:Unhandled exception in handleMsg:
title: pyOCD: pyocd gdbserver crashes when a serial terminal on a K64F is closed (macOS)
cause: On macOS closing a serial port sends a break, and DAPLink treats a serial break as a command to reset the target; pyocd does not expect the target to reset under it and fails reading registers.
fix: No fix in the thread: a DAPLink option to disable reset-on-break and reset detection in pyOCD were only proposed, and the issue still existed later. The reporter used OpenOCD instead, where the session stops but does not crash.

message: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x81 in position 0: invalid start byte
title: pyOCD: Semihosting binary file write raises UnicodeDecodeError
cause: SemihostAgent._get_string() decodes target data as UTF-8 regardless of whether the file was opened as binary, so non-UTF-8 binary data written via semihosting raises an exception.
fix: No fix in the thread. Maintainer and reporter agreed that _get_string() should return bytes and only text-mode files be encoded/decoded, and that target libraries (picolibc) should open files in binary mode by default.

message: invalid literal for int() with base 0:
title: pyOCD: File path containing '@' breaks flash/load
cause: The flash/load command treats an '@<address>' suffix on a file name as the load address, so a path containing '@' is split and the rest parsed as an integer.
fix: No fix in the thread; the maintainer planned to check whether a file with the full argument exists before processing the '@' suffix.

message: pylink.errors.JLinkException: No emulator with serial number 261002616 found.
title: pyOCD: J-Link probe with leading zeros in serial number is not found by pyocd
cause: The J-Link driver handles the serial number as an integer, so pyocd lists and matches J-Link probes without the leading zeros that the USB descriptor shows, and the zero-padded serial does not match. On Linux, opening a probe by the unique_id that pyocd itself reported (without zeros) still failed with 'No emulator with serial number ... found'; no cause was found for that.
fix: On macOS the maintainer could select the probe with the serial as pyocd list prints it (no leading zeros) or any unique part of it; this did not help the Linux API user, and the thread ends without a fix.

message: pyocd.core.exceptions.CoreRegisterAccessError: cannot write registers pc, r0, r1, r2, r9, sp, lr because core #0 is not halted
title: pyOCD: flashing a FRDM-K66F fails with core not halted when writing flash algorithm registers
cause: pyOCD timed out waiting for the core to halt after reset and then could not write the registers needed to call the flash algorithm. The maintainer wondered whether the device is locked, since connecting to locked devices had been troublesome; this was not confirmed.
fix: Suggested, not confirmed: add -M attach (connect mode attach) to the pyocd flash command.

message: uncaught exception: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'serial_number'
title: pyOCD: Picoprobe: exception when a probe UID is given but no Picoprobe is connected
cause: The Picoprobe enumeration code passes the result of a USB search to PicoLink without checking it, so it dereferences None when a probe UID is given but no Picoprobe is connected.
fix: The thread gives no confirmed fix.

message:
*** ERROR M201: test.svd (Line 28) 
  Tag <protection> unknown or not allowed on this level.
title: svdconv: SVDConv rejects protection tag inside addressBlock
cause: The protection element in addressBlock is part of the SVD schema since 1.3.2, but SVDConv 3.3.46 reports it as unknown on that level.
fix: The thread gives no confirmed fix.

title: cbuild: Function-like macro in define: is split into many -D options
cause: Without escaping or inner quotes the function-like define is split into separate -D tokens. Quoted forms reach the generated CMakeLists.txt intact, but CMake may then drop function-style definitions with a warning.
fix: Escape the characters (e.g. _LIBCPP_VERBOSE_ABORT\(\.\.\.\): \(\(void\)0\)) or use YAML quoting that keeps the inner quotes, e.g. - '"NAME(...)=((void)0)"'. The reporter's CMake (^3.25.2) accepted the macro; where CMake drops it, define the macro in a header file.

title: CMSIS Debugger: No "Show in Memory Inspector" entry in the Watch view
cause: The context menu entry needs VS Code 1.103 or newer, a Memory Inspector release that supports it, and a debug adapter that returns memory references for evaluated expressions. Support was missing in the Memory Inspector extension.
fix: Update the Memory Inspector extension to 1.3.0 or later; the entry then appears in the WATCH view. The variable name column in the Inspector still stays empty for such entries.

message: The custom reset command failed
title: CMSIS Debugger: Custom Reset button fails with "The custom reset command failed" while the target runs
cause: Custom Reset failed while the target was running; the maintainers tied it to the missing non-stop mode support.
fix: Pause the target before pressing Custom Reset. A CDT GDB Adapter change that halts the target before the reset (PR 464) was still in review at the end of the thread; it would not resume execution afterwards unless the customResetCommands do so.

title: CMSIS Solution: PROBLEMS view is empty while the status bar is red when Software Components view is open
cause: No cause in the thread: while the Software Components view was open, problems of the solution were not shown in the PROBLEMS view although the status bar indicated an error.
fix: Fixed in CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-04-21.

message:
*** ERROR M313: <pack>/./cmsis-pack/.build/<vendor>.<name>.pdsc (Line 30) 
  Associated File/Path is outside PACK root: 'src/include/lwfsm/'
title: packchk: ERROR M313 Associated File/Path is outside PACK root when pack paths contain ./
cause: packchk compares the canonical file path against the pack root with a plain string prefix check; a PDSC location containing ./ segments prevents the match, so valid files look outside the pack.
fix: A test fix that evaluates ./ and ../ in the path comparison was proposed (devtools-external PR 509); the thread does not show it merged or released.

title: pyOCD: Repeated flashing from a Linux VM randomly hangs
cause: Not determined. The reporter ran Ubuntu in VMware Player (it was also seen on Raspbian, not on Windows); the maintainer suspected the VM USB problem of #154, for which a timeout was added to the pyusb backend.
fix: Run `pyocd-tool -b <id> reset` before each flash command, which prevented the freeze for the reporter; the maintainer said the timeout added to the pyusb backend should fix it if it is the #154 problem.

title: pyOCD: Atmel EDBG CMSIS-DAP probe (SAMC21) not detected since pyocd 0.24
cause: Since pyocd 0.24.0 the Atmel EDBG CMSIS-DAP probe is not detected (0.23.0 detects it); the maintainer suspected changes to the checks for CMSIS-DAP names.
fix: Downgrade to pyocd 0.23.0 (adapting to its older Python API), which detects the probe. A pull request adding Atmel-ICE support (#991) might fix it too; not confirmed.

title: pyOCD: Programming several targets in parallel with pyOCD threads fails
cause: Each probe flashed fine on its own; a responder doubted that pyOCD's Python API can be used from several threads at once.
fix: Suggested, not confirmed: run the pyocd command line once per probe with that probe's unique ID, for example from a multiprocessing pool, instead of threads in one process.

title: pyOCD: RTT control block address and range cannot be set in the pyOCD YAML config
cause: At the time of the discussion the RTT settings existed only as command line options of the rtt command and were not session options, so putting them into the config file had no effect. Session options are listed in the options reference of the documentation.
fix: Pass the RTT control block address and size on the command line instead of the config file.

message: C Memory transfer fault @ 0x08000000-0x0800001f [__main__]
title: pyOCD: GD32 flashing fails with Memory transfer fault and SVD load ParseError
cause: The pack's SVD file failed to parse (the XML declaration was not at the start of the file); another user found that all SVDs of GigaDevice.GD32F30x_DFP 2.2.0 had whitespace before the XML declaration. The memory transfer fault at 0x08000000 was not explained: a built-in target with a hand-built memory map showed the same fault.
fix: Unpack the pack, fix the SVD files (strip the leading whitespace so the XML declaration starts the file), repack or pass the expanded folder with --pack, and report the issue to the vendor. This fixed the other user's pack; the reporter did not confirm it.

message: C No cores were discovered! [__main__]
title: pyOCD: nRF9160/nRF91x1 shows APPROTECT enabled and 'No cores were discovered' with older pyOCD
cause: pyOCD reports APPROTECT enabled on nRF91 devices (nRF9151/nRF9161 used with the nrf9160_xxaa target) although the user never enabled it, and unlocks by mass erase, which also wipes the settings storage. The thread gives no root cause. With pyOCD 0.35.1 the mass erase was followed by 'No cores were discovered'.
fix: To get loading working again, upgrade pyOCD (one user went from 0.35.1 to 0.39.0; the APPROTECT warning and mass erase still appear, but the load succeeds). An explicit chip erase (pyocd load -e chip, or pyocd erase -c) was also suggested. With the newer version, run the modem firmware update with -t nrf91.

message: C USB Error: [Errno 10060] Operation timed out [__main__]
title: pyOCD: 0.33.0: 'USB Error: Operation timed out' on pyocd list
cause: Appeared with v0.33.0, which newly provisioned libusb through the libusb-package dependency; v0.32.3 with a separately installed libusb worked. The maintainer could not reproduce it.
fix: Stay on v0.32.3; the maintainer planned v0.33.1 to revert the bundled libusb. Updating the ST-Link firmware helped one user only until the probe was replugged. Generic checks suggested: USB access rights, connect directly rather than via a hub, try another port or cable, make sure nothing else uses the device, try the system libusb.

message: C flash algorithm overflowed stack (4096 bytes) [__main__]
title: pyOCD: flash algorithm overflowed stack after converting a Keil FLM to a built-in target
cause: pyOCD programmed pages of 0x800 bytes (the sector size) although the FLASH_ALGO generated for STM32C031 gave 0x400, so the page buffers it used overlapped the flash algorithm's stack.
fix: Adjust the generated target so the stack does not overlap the page buffers: one user added 0x1000 to begin_stack and end_stack; another resized page_buffers for 0x800-byte pages and moved begin_stack and end_stack clear of them. Using the pack directly picked the correct page and sector sizes.

message: C target was not halted as expected after calling flash algorithm routine (IPSR=3) [__main__]
title: pyOCD: flash algorithm not halting (IPSR=3) when its RAM load address is invalid for the MCU
cause: The flash algorithm did not reach its expected halt. For one user with another chip the algorithm was loaded at 0x20000000, which is not valid memory on that MCU, so its init routine did not run correctly. For the LPC55S36 RevD1 board in the report the reporter suspected changes in the new chip ROM; that case stayed unsolved.
fix: Check that the flash algorithm is loaded into RAM that exists on the device and move its load address if not; that fixed it for the other user.

message: CRITICAL:__main__:Target type 'mimxrt0164cvl5a' not recognized.
title: pyOCD: Target type from a pack is 'not recognized' unless typed in uppercase
cause: A case-sensitive comparison somewhere in the pack target lookup, although pyOCD is meant to compare target types case-insensitively; the maintainer reproduced it with pyocd pack --find.
fix: Use the target name in upper case; the reporter changed the board's target name in pyocd/board/board_ids.py to upper case and the error went away.

message: Downloading packs (press Control-C to cancel):
title: pyOCD: pack install silently does nothing when index version differs from vendor pdsc
cause: The pack listed in the index has a newer version than what the vendor's pdsc or the download actually provides, so the expected version never appears locally and the part stays 'not installed'.
fix: Workaround reported: rename the locally cached pdsc to the version pyOCD expects (for example Holtek.HT32_DFP.1.0.75.pdsc to 1.0.76.pdsc). Retrying later worked for others once the versions matched.

message: ERROR:root:Unexpected exception: [Errno 10013] An attempt was made to access a socket in a way forbidden by its access permissions
title: pyOCD: gdbserver 'Errno 10013' socket access forbidden on Windows
cause: pyOCD could not bind the GDB port 3333, which points to another service holding that port (a maintainer saw this with a VPN client); for the reporter the problem later disappeared and its origin stayed unclear.
fix: Start the server on another port with -p (for example 3334); a server that then sits silently is just waiting for gdb to connect.

message: Flash pages (1024 bytes) do not fit evenly into sector (128 bytes)
title: pyOCD: AssertionError: flash pages do not fit evenly into sector (STM32L0/H7 Keil pack)
cause: The flash algorithm in the Keil STM32 device packs declares a page size larger than its sector size, which pyocd refuses.
fix: The pack's flash algorithm has to be fixed by the vendor: the maintainer reported it to Keil, who planned a fixed pack, and planned pyocd workarounds for such pack mistakes.

message: No cores were discovered!
title: pyOCD: ST-Link V3 connect to STM32F750 fails: 'AP wait' and no cores discovered
cause: A nominally identical second board worked, so the reporter put it down to a hardware fault on the first hand-soldered prototype; the maintainer notes Cortex-M7 STM32F7/H7 parts have been problematic and did not rule out an ST-Link V3 issue in pyOCD.
fix: Test with a second board or probe before suspecting pyOCD, and keep the ST-Link V3 firmware updated (early versions had bugs). Connecting under reset did not help here.

message: STLink error (5): No device connected
title: pyOCD: NUCLEO-H743ZI2 flash fails with STLink error (5) No device connected
cause: The ST-Link read the AP IDRs once and then failed on the second read with 'No device connected'; ST suggested the target may be running and going into a sleep mode after the initial connect.
fix: Retry with -Oconnect_mode=under-reset (or set connect_mode in pyocd.yaml); one participant reported this solved it, while the reporter still saw the failure with it on 0.25.0.

message: Target type stm32l431vctx not recognized. Use 'pyocd list --targets' to see currently available target types.
title: pyOCD: PyInstaller-built pyOCD app fails to open ST-Link session or lacks probes, targets
cause: pyOCD loads its probe drivers and RTOS plug-ins through package entry points, which PyInstaller does not collect by default, so the frozen app lacks them.
fix: In the .spec file use collect_entry_point('pyocd.probe') and collect_entry_point('pyocd.rtos') from PyInstaller.utils.hooks and add their datas and hidden imports. Also bundle the pyocd package folder as data and keep the _internal folder with the executable. A later 'target type not recognized' error with this setup stayed unresolved.

message: uncaught exception: /tmp/tmp1gi3hg44.so: wrong ELF class: ELFCLASS32
title: pyOCD: pyocd gdb fails loading the J-Link library with 'wrong ELF class: ELFCLASS32'
cause: pylink-square, used by pyOCD for J-Link probes, fails to load the SEGGER J-Link library while pyOCD looks for probes. The maintainer suspected a 32/64-bit mismatch; a later commenter found the library bitness made no difference and links it to a pylink-square library-loading problem on Linux (square/pylink#33).
fix: Uninstalling the J-Link software removed the error, but this disables J-Link probes in pyOCD; the maintainer also suggested reinstalling the J-Link driver package.

title: cbuild: IAR build error for Cortex-M55 when Dfpu is SP_FPU
cause: The IAR toolchain file mapped single-precision FPU to ERROR on Cortex-M55, but the hardware FPU there is double precision or none.
fix: Fixed by PR #1180 in the IAR toolchain mapping: SP_FPU now maps to the double-precision hardware on Cortex-M55 and M85. The thread names no release.

title: cbuild: CLANG build crashes or cannot find C headers with LLVM 17 for Cortex-M
cause: The CLANG toolchain file used an -mfpu option that crashes the compiler, a wrong CLANG_ARCH runtime folder, and explicit -isystem paths that did not find the standard headers.
fix: Use CMSIS-Toolbox 2.3.0-dev0 or later, confirmed to work with LLVM 17. Before that, the workaround was a CLANG cmake file without -mfpu that uses a sysroot option instead of the -isystem paths.

title: cbuild: cbuild clean fails with missing RTE files on a multi-target project
cause: Clean with cmsis-toolbox 2.6.0/2.6.1 depended on the files of all targets, so RTE files missing for a target that was never built caused errors and out and tmp were not cleaned. RTE files are meant to be kept in version control.
fix: A fix was provided in cbuild PR #343 (CMSIS-Toolbox nightly of 05.12.2024; proposed behaviour: delete tmpdir, and outdir only for the selected contexts), not confirmed by the reporter. Commit the RTE folder and run cbuild setup <solution> --packs; the reporter's own template change to the new compiler-selection format also made clean work.

title: cbuild: execute: step with always: seems skipped on the second build
cause: always: was honoured and the step did run (the log prints Executing: <context>-<execute name> unconditionally). The step runs CMake over the example's own FCARM/CMakeLists.txt, which checks dependencies and calls FCARM only when they require it.
fix: Nothing to fix in cbuild: always: works as documented, and whether FCARM is invoked is decided by the CMakeLists.txt that the execute step builds.

title: cbuild: Pre-build execute step output shows up after compiler output
cause: Ninja buffers the output of nested builds until the subprocess ends; with ninja --quiet on the nested build of an execute: step the pre-build output was reordered and appeared after the compiler output, although the step really ran first.
fix: Fixed in a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly build, confirmed by the reporter; the real order of execution was always correct.

title: cbuild: AC6 link step fails on map file option with quoted path (CMake 4.x, macOS)
cause: Quotation marks around the map file path, introduced by devtools PR #2129, ended up literally in the armlink --list option, so the link step broke.
fix: Fixed in the then latest CMSIS-Toolbox nightly; the reporter confirmed building with CMake 4.1.2 and a correctly generated map file. Update the toolbox.

title: cbuild: AC6 build tries to use /usr/bin/ld as linker on Linux
cause: CMake chooses the linker itself; the maintainer named a dirty CMake cache from an earlier misconfigured run as the likely reason the system /usr/bin/ld was picked instead of armlink, which was not confirmed.
fix: Set CMAKE_LINKER to the armlink path in the AC6.<version>.cmake toolchain file (confirmed by the reporter), or set LD to ${TOOLCHAIN_ROOT}/armlink${EXT}; cleaning the CMake cache with cbuild <project>.cprj --clear was suggested but not tested.

title: cbuild: AC6 build of a legacy armasm startup file fails on STM32F1 (GNU syntax assumed)
cause: armclang assembles with GNU syntax by default (-masm=gnu), but device startup files such as startup_stm32f10x_md.s use legacy armasm syntax.
fix: Add the assembler option -masm=auto under misc: ASM: (for example in cdefault.yml build-types). Note that the -masm option will be removed in a future Arm Compiler release.

title: cbuild: cbuild puts pack include paths before user paths, so duplicate headers shadow local ones
cause: csolution lists user add-paths first and pack paths after them in *.cbuild.yml, but cbuildgen ordered them the other way round, so a header present in a DFP shadowed a local copy.
fix: A fix of the include order in cbuild was decided. For modified DFP files the advised clean solution is a local pack: store the pack in the project and reference its pdsc instead of the installed one.

title: cbuild: IAR assembler error because the same define is passed globally and per file
cause: Defines add up through the hierarchy, so a define given both globally and for a single file appears twice on the command line, which the IAR assembler rejects.
fix: Do not repeat a global define at file level. The thread points to CMSIS-Toolbox 1.5.0 for the fix without saying which change it contains.

title: cbuild: IAR build fails because the preinclude file is passed with -include
cause: The IAR toolchain cmake file used the ArmClang option -include for pre-include files after PR #798 reverted the earlier fix; IAR needs --preinclude.
fix: As a local patch in IAR.<version>.cmake replace set(_PI "-include") with set(_PI "--preinclude "). IAR announced to include the correction in a pending toolchain file update; the thread shows no release.

title: cbuild: cbuild fails on macOS/Linux: empty cmake.in files missing after vcpkg install
cause: The tar extraction used by vcpkg artifacts on macOS and Linux dropped three empty files (CMakeTestAS_ARMCompiler.cmake.in, _GNUCompiler, _LEGCompiler) in the toolbox etc/CMakeASM folder, but cbuild needs them.
fix: Fixed for CMSIS-Toolbox 2.0.0-dev2 by putting a comment into the files so they are not empty.

title: cbuild: execute scripts do not run when building a single context
cause: executes nodes are only processed on full application builds; --context builds one project only, and for-context is only valid in cproject files (solution-level executes run once).
fix: Build with --context-set but without --context, or without any context option. Place execute nodes in the cproject.yml when they must run per context with for-context.

title: cbuild: Files in nested groups are compiled without -g and -O options
cause: cbuild 2.6.1 did not pass the -g and -O compile options to files placed in nested sub-groups, so no debug info was produced and breakpoints could not be set.
fix: Use a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly with the fix, which the reporter confirmed; no release is named. Until then keep such files out of nested groups.

title: cbuild: armclang compiler check fails in CI: no target architecture and later permission denied
cause: With CMSIS-Toolbox 2.4.0 the compiler check ran armclang without a target; with 2.9.0 the target was passed but the check still failed. The ultimate cause was the functional-safety variant of Arm Compiler 6, which needs an MDK Professional licence, while the reporter used a community licence.
fix: Update the toolbox, check the setup with `cbuild list environment` and `cbuild list toolchains -v`, and use the regular Arm Compiler 6.22 instead of the FuSa variant unless an MDK Professional licence is available.

title: cbuild: $SolutionDir()$ and $ProjectDir()$ in execute steps expand with extra ../ when -O is used
cause: A bug in cbuild2cmake made $SolutionDir()$ and $ProjectDir()$ in execute steps expand with an extra ../ component when cbuild's -O option was used.
fix: Use a toolbox nightly that contains the cbuild2cmake fix (PR #381), which the reporter confirmed; no release is named.

message:
*** ERROR M204:
  Path not found: '<packs>/GigaDevice/GD32F10x_DFP/2.0.3/Device\Include'!
title: cbuild: Path not found with backslashes in include path of a pack on macOS or Linux
cause: The pack's pdsc uses backslashes in file and include paths, which are not valid paths on macOS; packchk reports them as M327.
fix: Report it to the pack vendor, or edit the installed pdsc to use forward slashes (the reporter confirmed this works).

message:
*** ERROR M204:
  Path not found: 'C:/Temp/csolution_test/reproducer/white_space/RTE/Device/ARMCM3/ARMCM3_ac6.sct'!
title: cbuild: ERROR M204 path not found when a custom rtedir contains a space
cause: cbuildgen replaces spaces in the RTE path with underscores (meant for component classes such as 'CMSIS Driver') and also did so for spaces above the RTE folder, so a custom rtedir containing a space pointed to a path that does not exist.
fix: The tool was changed to replace only spaces below the RTE folder; with a version lacking the change, keep spaces out of the rtedir path.

message:
*** ERROR M207: <pack root>\Keil\ARM_Compiler\1.6.3\Keil.ARM_CompilerX.pdsc
  PDSC file name mismatch!
title: cbuild: cbuildgen rejects a pack whose pdsc file name differs from the pack name
cause: The pdsc file name must be <Vendor>.<Name>.pdsc (packchk reports M207 otherwise); csolution was more lenient than cbuildgen.
fix: Rename the pdsc to match the pack name. The maintainer believed the tools were aligned by CMSIS-Toolbox 1.1.0 and asked for a test; not confirmed.

message:
*** ERROR M800:
  RTE Model reports: Error R821: Required pack not installed
title: cbuild: ERROR M800 R821 Required pack not installed for a pack registered in local_repository.pidx
cause: Locally referenced packs were not supported by the early build tools.
fix: Support for local packs was added in devtools PR #33 (verified by the reporter on the main branch); use a tool version that contains it.

message: -- Configuring done (188.5s)
title: cbuild: CMake configuration step takes minutes with Arm Compiler 6
cause: Most likely latency of the floating license server used with Arm Compiler 6 during CMake's compiler identification; with GCC configuration takes about 3 s.
fix: MDK v6 uses user-based licensing, with which this latency should not appear any more. Compiler detection can be skipped, and CMake caches the configuration so later runs are faster.

message:
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:43:
  Parse error.  Function missing ending ")".  Instead found bad character
  with text "\".
title: cbuild: Build with an old pack fails on Linux and macOS because of backslashes in paths
cause: Older packs have backslashes in path names, which csolution passed unchanged into the generated CMake file; on Linux and macOS this breaks the CMake syntax.
fix: Use a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly from 2024-12-10 or later, with which the example builds on Linux; the request was that csolution converts backslashes to forward slashes.

message: CMake Error: The source "<tmp>/Demo.Debug+MyBoard/CMakeLists.txt" does not match the source "<tmp>/Demo.Debug+AVH/CMakeLists.txt" used to generate cache.
title: cbuild: CMake error that the cache source does not match after switching the target type
cause: After the active target type changed, the CMake cache in tmp still belonged to the previous context, so CMake refused the new source directory.
fix: Use a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly from 2024-12-09 or later: switching the target type now cleans the context and sets it up again.

message: E: bad pack name: it should be one of the following formats: Vendor.Pack, Vendor.Pack.x.y.z, Vendor.Pack.x.y.z.pack, or Vendor.Pack.pdsc
title: cbuild: cbuild prints 'bad pack name' from cpackget with --context-set
cause: A regression in the 2.5.0 pre-release (2.5.0-devint5): with --context-set, the output of csolution list packs began with an info line about cbuild-set.yml, which cbuild passed to cpackget as a pack name.
fix: Fixed in a cbuild PR, validated on Windows; the maintainers aimed to ship it before the 2.5.0 release.

message: ERROR M204: Path not found: c:\projectpath\RTE\_Target_1
title: cbuild: ERROR M204 on RTE/_Target_1 for a project converted from uVision with no build-type
cause: A converted solution with target-types but no build-type makes csolution generate RTE/_<target-type> while cbuildgen 1.5.0 expects a phantom RTE/_Target_1. cbuild also no longer modifies the RTE directory by default.
fix: Workaround: declare a build-type in csolution.yml (build-types: - type: any), or create the missing RTE/_Target_1 directory. Making target-type mandatory was discussed.

message: Error: L6200E: Symbol func multiply defined (by test.o and test.o).
title: cbuild: Linker error for symbol defined twice when two components reference the same source file
cause: Two components of the pack list the same source file. cbuild2cmake compiles it for each component and the linker reports duplicate symbols, while the RteModel and cbuildgen silently dropped the duplicate and hid the problem.
fix: Treat it as a component design error in the pack and let only one selected component contribute the file, for example through a common component the others depend on; packchk is to detect such packs (devtools #1499).

message: Error: L6218E: Undefined symbol osRtxThreadStackCheck (referred from irq_armv7m.o).
title: cbuild: Undefined symbol osRtxThreadStackCheck after turning off RTX stack overrun checking
cause: No dependency flags were passed for armclang ASM files, so the assembly source had no recorded dependency on RTX_Config.h and was not reassembled after the configuration change.
fix: Rebuild the solution as a workaround. The maintainer proposed setting the ASM dependency flags in the AC6 build configuration, and the reporter confirmed that a later toolbox nightly fixes it; no release is named.

message: error cbuild: error cleaning '<project>/<name>.cbuild-idx.yml'
title: cbuild: cbuild --rebuild cannot remove tmp directory
cause: The tmp directory was open as the working directory of a Bash shell, so with CMSIS-Toolbox 2.6.1 the rebuild could not delete it on Windows.
fix: Leave the tmp directory in the shell before rebuilding; with the changed cleanup strategy of CMSIS-Toolbox 2.7.0 (cbuild PR #343) the same steps no longer give an error.

message: error csolution: specified regions header was not found
title: cbuild: 2.7.0 rejects linker regions header that an executes step generates
cause: csolution 2.7.0 checks the regions header before the build, so a file produced by an executes node does not exist yet (2.6.1 only warned).
fix: Create the file beforehand (touch) as a workaround. Devtools PR 1921 treats it like user files; it was merged for the next nightly build and the reporter confirmed the fix; no release is named.

message: info cbuild: build finished successfully!
title: cbuild: Build succeeds but no .axf produced when only a legacy armasm file exists
cause: The AS_ARM language used for legacy armasm files had no link rule in the AC6 CMake description, so linking produced no .axf and reported no error.
fix: Fixed in devtools PR 1101; the workaround was appending a CMAKE_AS_ARM_LINK_EXECUTABLE armlink rule to the AC6.<version>.cmake file.

message: info cbuild: missing packs must be installed, rerun cbuild with the --packs option
title: cbuild: Local pack version read from the pidx instead of the pdsc; cbuild asks for a pack
cause: cbuildgen read the version of a locally referenced pack from the local_repository.pidx entry, which becomes stale when the pdsc version changes.
fix: Workaround: update the version in local_repository.pidx to match the pdsc. Fixes for cbuildgen packlist (PR #442) and the exit code (cbuild PR #9) were offered for testing in CMSIS-Toolbox 1.1.0, not confirmed in the thread.

message: ld.exe: final link failed: no symbols
title: cbuild: GCC link fails for a Secure project without non-secure callable entries
cause: GCC cannot generate a CMSE import library when the secure project has no non-secure callable entry functions and fails the link; AC6 only warns.
fix: Set secure-only in the trustzone: node under processor:, so no import library is generated for that project; validated with the CMSIS-Toolbox nightly of 2024-09-03.

message: ninja: error: '.../out/CM33_s/AVH/Debug/CM33_s_CMSE_Lib.o', needed by '.../out/CM33_ns/AVH-NS-only/Debug/CM33_ns.elf', missing and no known rule to make it
title: cbuild: cbuild --rebuild --active removes secure outputs needed by the non-secure target
cause: Two separate effects. In the reported project the target-set of the non-secure-only target pointed at the Release project context while the Debug set was selected, so the wrong context was built. In addition, --rebuild with --active cleans all contexts, not only those of the selected target-set, which deletes the prebuilt secure artifacts that the non-secure image consumes.
fix: Make each target-set reference the project contexts of its own build type (CM33_ns.Debug in the Debug set). Building the non-secure context directly with --context does not remove the secure artifacts. The --rebuild cleaning behaviour has no fix in the thread.

title: CMSIS-Core: CoreDebug_Type is gone in CMSIS 6, breaking vendor SDK code
cause: CMSIS 6 renamed the CoreDebug_Type structure to DCB_Type, which breaks vendor code such as NXP's fsl_common.c.
fix: Use DCB_Type; the issue was marked as addressed by PR #122 without saying what it changes or which release has it.

title: CMSIS-Core: SCB_VTOR_TBLOFF_Msk differs from the vendor manual
cause: CMSIS implements VTOR.TBLOFF as the Armv7-M architecture specifies it (mask 0xFFFFFF80); implementers such as ST may restrict the implemented bits and require stronger alignment (512 bytes on this STM32).
fix: Align the vector table as the device manual requires; CMSIS cannot encode implementation specifics.

title: CMSIS-Core: __disable_irq() returns void in CMSIS 6, code relying on the old return value breaks
cause: Older Arm Compiler support (arm_compat.h) declared __disable_irq() as returning the previous mask state. When the include of arm_compat.h was dropped from the CMSIS toolchain headers, the CMSIS variant kept only the void signature, so code that saved the return value to restore interrupts later no longer builds.
fix: With Arm Compiler, include arm_compat.h explicitly to get the signature with the return value. The maintainer considers bringing the return value back in CMSIS and asked for a pull request; no change or release is shown.

message: Error[Pe2529]: _Noreturn is not allowed here
title: CMSIS-Core: IAR rejects __NO_RETURN in a function pointer typedef
cause: For IAR the macro maps to the C11 _Noreturn keyword (since CMSIS_6 PR #85), which is not allowed in a function pointer type.
fix: Use __attribute__((__noreturn__)) directly in the typedef (needs language extensions on IAR). The maintainers planned to use the attribute when __has_attribute reports it and asked the reporter to check PR #284; no confirmation in the thread.

message: Include/cmsis_gcc.h:28: error: ignoring '#pragma clang system_header' [-Werror=unknown-pragmas]
title: CMSIS-Core: cmsis_gcc.h: #pragma clang system_header gives an error with -Werror
cause: A clang pragma was left in the GCC header cmsis_gcc.h, which GCC rejects under -Werror=unknown-pragmas.
fix: Replace it with `#pragma GCC system_header` in cmsis_gcc.h, as proposed in PR #141; no merge or release is shown.

message: warning: array subscript 'uint64_t {aka long long unsigned int}[0]' is partly outside array bounds of 'uint32_t[1]' {aka 'long unsigned int[1]'} [-Warray-bounds=]
title: CMSIS-Core: GCC -Warray-bounds warning from __TZ_set_STACKSEAL_S in startup file
cause: The linker symbol __StackSeal is 64 bit but was declared as uint32_t in the startup template.
fix: Declare __STACK_SEAL as extern uint64_t in the startup file; the reporter opened PRs for the CMSIS_6 template (#260) and for Cortex_DFP (#22).

title: CMSIS Debugger: Target stays halted after disconnect with pyOCD
cause: The adapter killed the GDB server immediately, before pyOCD could turn off debug and resume the CPU.
fix: Use a CDT GDB Adapter with the server kill delay (PRs 405 and 175), which together with automaticallyKillServer gives pyOCD time to disconnect cleanly; it was tested with a not yet public build, no release named. Until then, reset or power-cycle the board after disconnecting.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Debugger hangs when more breakpoints are set than hardware allows
cause: GDB accepts all and fails at continue with "Command aborted" after sending ^running; the adapter had already dropped the command.
fix: Keep the number of breakpoints within the hardware limit (an improved error message asks to remove breakpoints). A CDT GDB Adapter fix for the late error (PR 415) was implemented but still needed tests; no release is named. Possible workaround: 'set breakpoint always-inserted on' in initCommands, which however uncovers other breakpoint management issues.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Memory reads and views fail while the CPU runs (SIGINT interrupts)
cause: GDB suppresses remote commands while the target runs; non-stop mode did not work well with RTOS threads.
fix: Use pyOCD 0.40.0 with CDT GDB Adapter 2.4.0 or later: pyOCD's GDB server accepts several clients on one port (PR 1835), so an auxiliary GDB connection reads memory while the main connection keeps run control.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Misleading error for attach request when no GDB server runs
cause: The adapter passed through GDB messages, which differ by OS (a drive-joining text on Windows, a timeout text on macOS).
fix: Start the GDB server before the attach request. PR 413 of the CDT GDB Adapter aligns the Windows message with the clearer macOS one; it was tested during review, no release is named.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Generated J-Link launch configuration on macOS uses JLinkGDBServerCLExe
cause: The debug adapter template generated the server name JLinkGDBServerCLExe on macOS, whereas JLinkGDBServerCL is more stable there; Load & Run was affected as well.
fix: Use a CMSIS Solution build with the updated debug adapter registry (PR 45, merged; validated with an internal build from main, no release named), or change the server name in launch.json to JLinkGDBServerCL.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Breakpoints cannot be set in assembler files
cause: Breakpoints could not be set in assembler files because the CDT GDB Adapter extension declared no language for them; a pseudo-language definition in that extension enables them.
fix: Use a CDT GDB Adapter release that contains the merged pseudo-language definition for assembler (cdt-gdb-vscode PR 191); it was announced for the next release, presumably 2.5.0.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Component Viewer shows current instead of maximum stack with OS_STACK_WATERMARK
cause: The numeric conversion of the string returned by GDB for the values was wrong, so current and maximum came out identical on some devices (seen with the RTX library on Microchip and ST hardware).
fix: Use a CMSIS Debugger build containing PR 854 (merged and confirmed working with a CI build; no release named).

title: CMSIS Debugger: Component Viewer stays empty when one SCVD file is missing or invalid
cause: One unreadable SCVD (missing file, broken path in the cbuild-run file, syntax error) made the whole view fail instead of only that component.
fix: Use a CMSIS Debugger build in which unreadable SCVD files are skipped and the other components are shown (implemented; no release named). Check the SCVD files and their paths in the cbuild-run file if a component is missing.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Component Viewer shows thread names as addresses while the target is running
cause: While the target ran, the Component Viewer showed thread names as addresses and showed the names again after a pause; the fix lets the viewer's GDB calls run without a frame ID, which points to those calls failing while the target runs.
fix: Use a CMSIS Debugger build with PR 835, which allows GDB calls with an undefined frameId and leaves them to the driver; no release is named. Pausing the target shows the names.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Connect fails with cbuild-run when CMSIS_PACK_ROOT is not set
cause: The pack-based support needed CMSIS_PACK_ROOT and the default was not applied.
fix: Set CMSIS_PACK_ROOT; the default locations per platform are documented in the CMSIS-Toolbox installation guide. Having the extension set the default when the variable is missing was proposed, not shown as done.

title: CMSIS Debugger: Run control becomes unresponsive while Component Viewer is open on a multi-core target
cause: Requests that the Component Viewer sent to GDB could leave the CDT GDB Adapter or GDB unresponsive while running and stepping; Reset Target did not always recover.
fix: Update to CMSIS Debugger 1.4.1 or later, which contains the fix (#888); error messages may still appear occasionally, but run control no longer hangs as easily.

message: Evaluation of expression without frameId is not supported.
title: CMSIS Debugger: GDB commands in Debug Console fail while CPU runs: no frameId
cause: The adapter required a frame for evaluation, which does not exist while running.
fix: Auxiliary GDB connections were implemented in PRs (cdt-gdb-adapter 449, cdt-gdb-vscode 181) that were still open at the end of the thread; they were tested with the J-Link, ST-Link (STM32CubeIDE) and OpenOCD GDB servers, which accept several connections on one port. Use an adapter that contains them; the thread names no release.

message: Failed to decode cstring '241 'ñ''. {}
title: CMSIS Debugger: Debug Console flooded by "Failed to decode cstring" while RTOS Views is open
cause: The CDT GDB Adapter failed to decode non-UTF-8 bytes in strings read for the RTOS view and logged each failure to the Debug Console.
fix: The fix was merged into the CDT GDB Adapter for its next release (expected to be 2.5.0); use a CMSIS Debugger that ships that adapter release.

message: GDB unhandled notify: breakpoint-created
title: CMSIS Debugger: "GDB unhandled notify: breakpoint-created" for breakpoints set from the console
cause: The adapter did not handle GDB breakpoint notifications, so CLI breakpoints did not show in the GUI.
fix: Use a CDT GDB Adapter extension release that handles the breakpoint-created notification; the thread announces it for the next release without naming a version.

message: Internal error: Failed to update peripheral GPIOA after memory reads: Attempt to access memory outside buffer bounds
title: CMSIS Debugger: GDB internal error at breakpoint and unreadable peripherals without a cbuild-run file
cause: The debugger ran standalone with a makefile build and no *.cbuild-run.yml, so the debug sequences of the device pack (on the STM32G474 the DBGMCU_CR setup) were missing, which can make memory and core register accesses fail; once a cbuild-run.yml was in place the GDB crash went away. The 'outside buffer bounds' error is a separate Peripheral Inspector bug.
fix: Provide a *.cbuild-run.yml. Without a CMSIS Solution build, create an example or blank solution for the board with the CMSIS Solution extension and reuse its generated *.cbuild-run.yml, *.dbgconf, launch.json and tasks.json, adjusted to your build output.

title: RTX: osKernelInitialize fails because osRtxInfo memory is all 0xFF at startup
cause: The deprecated LPC1700_DFP was not compatible with the CMSIS-Toolbox, which generated a faulty scatter file, so the stack was broken before startup.
fix: Not spelled out in the thread: the reporter traced the problem to the scatter file generated from the deprecated LPC1700_DFP and closed the issue.

title: CMSIS Solution: Outline: removing a file from a layer leaves the clayer.yml entry
cause: File items in the outline tree did not get the layerUri attribute, so removing a file from a layer deleted the file but left its reference in the clayer.yml.
fix: Fixed (verified in the thread): removing a file from the Solution Outline also removes its .clayer.yml entry; no build or release is named.

title: CMSIS Solution: Changes to cmsis-csolution.environmentVariables are not seen by the running RPC server
cause: The RPC daemon kept the environment it was started with, so changes to cmsis-csolution.environmentVariables only reached processes started afterwards.
fix: Fixed (validated with CI artifacts): changing a value in cmsis-csolution.environmentVariables now restarts the RPC server.

title: CMSIS Solution: Loading Solution never ends after modifying debug-adapters.yml
cause: A modified debug-adapters.yml led to runtime errors in processing the debug adapter registry that were apparently not caught; the maintainer assumed loading only completes once the tasks.json and launch.json update does, so loading never ended.
fix: Fixed by #199: the solution loads and the problem is reported the usual VS Code way.

title: CMSIS Solution: Software Components list incomplete when opened a second time with a repository-local pack
cause: A csolution RPC bug, fixed in devtools PR 2394: when Manage Software Components was opened a second time, only the selected components were listed.
fix: Fixed by devtools PR 2394, verified against the latest csolution RPC build and included in the latest devtools nightly at the time.

title: CMSIS Solution: Pack lock cannot be removed after switching from a local to a released pack
cause: After a local repository was used for ARM::SDS@3.0.0-dev (which created its entry in cbuild-pack.yml) and the released pack was then installed, the pack lock could not be removed and the installed pack was shown incorrectly; the thread names no root cause and suspects it was fixed along with #250.
fix: Use CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-06-10 or later; then the lock can be resolved and the installed version selected.

title: CMSIS Solution: Build after a target change in Manage Solution produces no output files
cause: With an unsaved target change from Manage Solution, Build saved the changes and started cbuild and cbuild setup concurrently (the database generation had been split off from cbuild setup); when cbuild finished first, the later setup removed its outputs.
fix: Use CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-06-10 or later; with VS Code set to save files before running a task, Build now saves the files and runs csolution convert before building. On older versions save explicitly before building.

title: CMSIS Solution: Outline view shows no files for a Zephyr/West project when first opened
cause: For Zephyr/West projects the *.cbuild.yml file list is completed only during cbuild setup from compile_commands.json, but the Outline view was refreshed right after solution conversion.
fix: The extension now refreshes the Outline after cbuild setup for Zephyr/West projects; validated with CI artifacts, no release named.

title: CMSIS Solution: Solution is not converted after a generator creates the cgen.yml file
cause: The extension did not react when a generator created the missing .cgen.yml, so no solution convert followed.
fix: Use the CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-09-09 or later; there cbuild setup runs once the generator has finished.

message: ERROR: Input redirection is not supported, exiting the process immediately.
title: CMSIS Solution: Generator start floods output with 'Input redirection is not supported'
cause: The generator's Windows launch script contained TIMEOUT statements, which probably produce the repeated error when the extension starts the generator; the cgen.yml was still written and the application built.
fix: Use the CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-06-09 or later, which bundles a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly with the updated generator launch script.

message: NoPermissions (FileSystemError): Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, scandir 'c:\GitRepos\REPO_NAME\.pytest_cache'
title: CMSIS Solution: CMSIS View stuck on 'Loading' when a VS Code workspace has additional folders
cause: Activation of the extension failed when its solution roots watcher tried to read a workspace folder it had no permission for (EPERM on a .pytest_cache folder), so the CMSIS View stayed on Loading.
fix: Use the CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-07-01 or later, which the reporter confirmed resolves it.

message: board 'KIT_T2G-B-H_LITE:V1' was not found
title: CMSIS Solution: Saving Software Components strips packs/components from other contexts' clayer files
cause: Saving the Software Components view for one context removed the packs: and components: nodes from .clayer.yml files used only by other contexts, so their board layer no longer referenced the BSP/DFP packs.
fix: Fixed in a CMSIS Solution CI build after 1.68.0 (validated from CI artifacts); no release is named.

message: error csolution: unknown selected context(s):
title: CMSIS Solution: Loading Solution never stops when the csolution lists a project file that does not exist
cause: A csolution.yml that lists a project file that does not exist left the load process hanging, so Loading Solution never stopped.
fix: Fixed: the outline now shows 'Solution cannot be loaded' instead of Loading (validated with the CMSIS Solution nightly of 2026-03-23).

title: cpackget: Two different default pack folders on macOS (gen-pack vs cpackget)
cause: gen-pack looked in a different default than cpackget; the default is ~/.cache/arm/packs (all lower case, with a dot) on macOS and Linux, and XDG_CACHE_HOME is honoured by cpackget.
fix: Use a gen-pack with the aligned default (gen-pack#37). If the pack folder has a different case, remove ~/.cache/arm and let cpackget recreate it; setting CMSIS_PACK_ROOT explicitly avoids relying on the defaults.

title: cpackget: cpackget update-index -a leaves some pdsc files missing in .Web
cause: The concurrent download scheduler spawned more workers than configured and did not wait for the last ones, so some downloaded files were cut off or never moved to .Web.
fix: Use a cpackget with the semaphore-based download scheduler; the thread names no release. Workaround: run update-index -a -C 0 to disable concurrent downloads.

title: cpackget: cpackget add fails because pack IDs were matched case-sensitively
cause: cpackget looked up pack IDs case-sensitively, so cpackget add ARM::ethos-u-core-driver@1.24.8, the pack ID a project referenced, did not find the pack.
fix: Use a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly build from 2025-04-10 or later, whose cpackget looks up pack IDs case-insensitively; no release is named.

title: cpackget: cpackget add of an older pack version fails with 'URL for the pack cannot be determined'
cause: cpackget looked up the pdsc entry in index.pidx by vendor, name and the requested version, but the index lists only the latest version of each pack, so an older version cannot be found while its pdsc is not yet in .Web. It should look up vendor and name only.
fix: Install the latest version of the pack first, so that its pdsc lands in .Web; the older version then installs. PR #60 changes the lookup to vendor and name.

message: E: "https://mcuxpresso.nxp.com/cmsis_pack/repo/NXP.MCXN947_DFP.19.0.0.pack": bad request
title: cpackget: cpackget download of an NXP pack fails with 404 although curl works
cause: The NXP pack server answered 404 to requests with the User-Agent cpackget/v2.1.5, while the same download with a generic Go User-Agent worked; a cpackget change (PR 359) was suspected as the regression.
fix: NXP fixed the problem on their side, and the thread's wording ('also fixed') suggests a cpackget change as well without naming it; retry the download.

message: E: "https://www.geehy.com/uploads/tool/Geehy.APM32A0xx_DFP.1.0.0.pack": failed to download file
title: cpackget: cpackget add fails to download a pack from a server that sets cookies
cause: The pack server answers a plain client with a JavaScript redirect page and serves the file only once a cookie has been set, so a client without cookie handling never gets the pack although a browser does.
fix: Fixed by cookie support in cpackget, seen in cpackget 2.1.5-6-gd958da1 from the CMSIS-Toolbox nightly 2.6.1-38; update the toolbox. In that nightly a failed cbuild setup also no longer writes cbuild-run.yml.

message: E: "https://www.keil.com/pack/keil.vidx": remote server is offline or cannot be reached
title: cpackget: cpackget init: 'remote server is offline or cannot be reached' though browser works
cause: Before downloading, cpackget checks the connection by fetching the Keil.vidx index; the error means that download failed. In the reported case the DNS configuration was broken: /etc/resolv.conf was empty on a system using systemd-resolved, although curl requests to the pack URLs worked. Proxy settings and missing CA certificates were suggested as other possible causes.
fix: Fix the name resolution, for example on systemd-resolved link /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf to /etc/resolv.conf. Otherwise test the keil.com pack URLs with curl -L and check HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY and the CA store, as the maintainers suggested. Not a cpackget defect.

message: E: A pack in the cache folder has malformed pack name: C:.CMSIS_PACKS.ARM.CMSIS-Driver.2.6.1.pack
title: cpackget: cpackget list fails in git-bash with 'Pack vendor "" does not match' and lists nothing
cause: In git-bash/MinGW a CMSIS_PACK_ROOT such as /c/CMSIS_PACKS reaches cpackget as C:/CMSIS_PACKS with forward slashes, and cpackget list then fails to parse the installed pack paths. An unquoted C:\PACKS in export or -R also loses its backslashes, which bash treats as escape characters, and becomes C:PACKS.
fix: Set the pack root with doubled backslashes (export CMSIS_PACK_ROOT=c:\\CMSIS_PACKS) or quote it (cpackget -R "C:\PACKS").

message: E: Can't decompress "<packs>\.Download\Keil.STM32F1xx_DFP.2.4.0.pack": zip: not a valid zip file
title: cpackget: cpackget add behind a VPN/proxy fails and later errors with 'zip: not a valid zip file'
cause: The proxy was not configured the way cpackget expects; with the http_proxy environment variable set (see cpackget's 'working behind a proxy' notes) the download works. The failed download left a 0-byte pack in .Download that was reused on the next run instead of downloaded again, because cpackget only removed the file when unzipping failed.
fix: Set http_proxy for the shell and delete the empty pack file from .Download. PR #69 removes the file after HTTP errors too, expected in the next release.

message: E: Can't move file "<packs>\.Download\index.pidx" to "<packs>\.Web\index.pidx": rename ... Access is denied.
title: cpackget: cpackget index/update-index fails with 'Access is denied' when index.pidx is read-only
cause: Files in the pack root are meant to be read-only. The folder had been set up by MDK's Pack Installer, and cpackget could not overwrite its read-only index.pidx.
fix: Remove the read-only attribute from the files in the pack root.

message: E: Get "https://itools.infineon.com/cmsis_packs/T2G-B-H/Infineon.T2G-B-H_DFP.1.2.1.pack": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
title: cpackget: cpackget add: 'certificate signed by unknown authority' on old Debian image
cause: The pack server's certificate chain ends in a root CA that is missing from the CA store of that Debian 12 image (wget fails too; Debian 13 and Ubuntu work). It is a host trust-store problem, not a pack problem.
fix: Use an OS image whose CA store trusts the issuing root (the error did not occur on Debian 13 or Ubuntu Server 24.04). Otherwise use a cpackget with the --insecure-skip-verify option, at your own risk: cpackget add <pack> --insecure-skip-verify (verified with a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly build; the CMSIS-Toolbox release tested before lacked the option).

message: E: fail to create directory
title: cpackget: cpackget add: 'mkdir ...: permission denied' in a non-writable working directory
cause: cpackget created a temporary pdsc working folder relative to the current working directory instead of the system temp directory.
fix: Run cpackget from a writable working directory, or use a cpackget with the fix that creates the temporary folder under os.TempDir(); the thread names no release.

message: E: fail to decompress file
title: cpackget: cpackget add fails with 'zip: not a valid zip file' (corrupt cached pack)
cause: The pack file cached in .Download was damaged by a failed download, and cpackget used that cached file.
fix: Run cpackget rm --purge ARM::CMSIS@6.1.0 to drop the cached pack, then cpackget add ARM::CMSIS@6.1.0 again; if it still fails, rerun with -v to get a log.

message: E: failed to download file
title: cpackget: cpackget init fails with 'no such host' behind a proxy after a toolbox update
cause: cpackget 0.8.0 (toolbox 1.1.0) has a bug in its proxy handling, while 0.7.0 worked through the same proxy. For https URLs only HTTPS_PROXY applies, and it needs a proxy with a valid certificate; HTTP_PROXY has no effect.
fix: Set HTTPS_PROXY to the proxy (with a valid certificate). For the 0.8.0 proxy bug the maintainer offered a test build v0.8.1-alpha.1 from a personal fork, not confirmed in the thread; cpackget 0.7.0 from toolbox 1.0.0 still worked for the reporter.

message: E: file not found
title: cpackget: Installing a local .pack with spaces in the path fails with bad pack name
cause: The MDK Pack Installer (uVision 5.39) called cpackget without quoting the pack path, so a path containing a space was split into two arguments.
fix: Not a cpackget defect: cpackget add "<path with spaces>\Vendor.Pack.1.0.0.pack" with quotes works. The Pack Installer bug is tracked against MDK; meanwhile use the PackInstaller of MDK 5.38a or the updated version from knowledge article KA005531.

message: E: invalid dimensions
title: cpackget: cpackget add prints 'E: invalid dimensions' in a very small terminal window
cause: The license text is shown in a text window that needs a minimum terminal size. If the terminal (for example a VS Code panel reduced to a few lines) is smaller, the UI library fails with this cryptic message.
fix: Enlarge the terminal to at least 50 columns by 8 rows and repeat the command. The cpackget nightly 2.1.8-45-g83198e5 (2025-09-10) checks the size first and prints 'increase window size to display license information and obtain user response to at least 50x8'.

message: E: open <packs>\ARM.CMSIS-Compiler.2.2.0-dev24+g3f9552c\ARM.CMSIS-Compiler.pdsc: The system cannot find the path specified.
title: cpackget: Local pack with +build version keeps metadata; rm fails when pdsc is gone
cause: cpackget copied the full version including +meta into local_repository.pidx and, on rm without a version, tried to read the missing pdsc to learn the version instead of just matching vendor and pack name.
fix: Use a cpackget newer than 2.2.0 with the change (validated with build 2.2.0-4-g487974c): meta information is stripped on add, and rm removes the local_repository entry even when the pdsc file no longer exists. Otherwise remove the entry from local_repository.pidx by hand or put the pdsc file back.

message: E: pack not installed
title: cpackget: Cannot remove a local pack entry whose pdsc file was deleted
cause: A pack registered via its pdsc file stays in .Local/local_repository.pidx after the pdsc is deleted. In the report, removing by packID with the version failed, and the attempt by pdsc path had a typo (.pds instead of .pdsc).
fix: Remove the entry with cpackget rm using the packID without version (for example ARM::SDS) or the exact pdsc path as shown by cpackget list; both worked in the maintainer's test with cpackget 2.2.1 although the pdsc no longer existed. Deleting the pdsc line from local_repository.pidx by hand also works. The maintainers added a note to the documentation and made no tool change.

message: E: pack version is not the latest in the pdsc file
title: cpackget: cpackget add of a BSP fails to install required packs: 'does not match pack version ""'
cause: Regression in cpackget 2.1.1: for dependencies of the form >=x.y.z cpackget uses an internal open upper bound (x.y.z:_) that the range comparison did not support, and the version and range arguments were swapped in the modifier resolution.
fix: Use a cpackget newer than 2.1.1 that contains both corrections; version 2.0.1 still installed the requirements correctly.

message: E: pack version not found in the pdsc file
title: cpackget: cpackget add ARM::CMSIS@6.0.0+meta fails with 'pack version not found in the pdsc file'
cause: Build metadata after + must be ignored for comparison (SemVer), but cpackget compared it literally against the releases in the pdsc. Packs differing only in metadata are the same version and share one install folder.
fix: Use a cpackget with PR #273 (validated in a CI build), or leave the +meta part out of the pack specification.

message: E: pack version not found in the pdsc file
title: cpackget: cpackget add of a newly published pack: 'pack version not found in the pdsc file'
cause: The local .Web/index.pidx and pdsc are older than the publication of that pack version, so the requested release is not listed yet.
fix: Run cpackget update-index and repeat. In the CMSIS-Toolbox nightly of 2024-12-09, cpackget add refreshes an outdated index and downloads the missing pdsc itself; no release is named.

message: E: pack version not found in the pdsc file
title: cpackget: cpackget add .pack: 'has no release tag matching version' with older local pdsc
cause: cpackget checked the requested version against the pdsc already registered in .Local (local_repository.pidx) before extracting the pdsc of the pack being installed.
fix: Remove the pack's entry from local_repository.pidx before installing the pack file; the maintainer said he would fix the check.

message: E: pack version not found in the pdsc file
title: cpackget: cpackget add: 'pack version not found' for versions like 2.0.0-alpha.0.5
cause: The semantic-version expression taken from the pack index specification had a repeating capture group that returned a variable number of matches for dotted pre-release parts, which broke version splitting.
fix: Use a cpackget release after 0.4.1 with the merged bugfix; a matching correction of the specification's regex was proposed.

message: E: pdsc not found
title: cpackget: cpackget add reports 'pdsc not found' inside a freshly downloaded pack
cause: An old pdsc of the pack in the .Web folder was no longer being updated, so cpackget did not find the expected pdsc in the downloaded pack.
fix: Delete the outdated pdsc of that pack from .Web and add the pack again; the issue was later marked verified without naming a release.

message: The system cannot find the path specified.
title: cpackget: cpackget add of a local pdsc registers a wrong path (no drive letter, C: vs c:)
cause: On Windows, cpackget add with a pdsc path that starts with a backslash but has no drive letter stored a wrong path built from the current directory. An upper-case drive letter also produced a 'malformed path' warning and a reinstall, while a lower-case one did not.
fix: Give the full pdsc path including the drive letter. A later cpackget handles lower- and upper-case drive letters; the thread names no version.

message: panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1
title: cpackget: cpackget add panics 'index out of range' for pre-release versions like -alpha.1.9
cause: cpackget 0.9.2 crashed while checking the pack's requirements because a required pack version with a complex pre-release part (2.0.0-alpha.1.9) did not fit its internal version representation; 0.9.0 installed the pack.
fix: Skip dependency installation with the -n flag until a patched cpackget is available.

message: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
title: cpackget: cpackget add crashes with a nil pointer for a local pack whose url is a file:/// location
cause: cpackget's FileExists() crashed because the file info returned by os.Stat was nil when adding a local pack whose pdsc gives a file:/// url.
fix: Use a cpackget with the corrected FileExists(); the thread names no release.

title: csolution: Component with older API major version gets the wrong API from the newest pack
cause: With two versions of a pack loaded, the newest one always wins when no version is given, so a component implementing API 0.1.0 was built against the incompatible API 1.0.0.
fix: Fixed by PR #1130: the API resolves to the highest available version inside the major version the component requires (at least the required one); an error is raised if none fits, and a conflict error if selected components require different major versions. The thread names no release.

title: csolution: cbuild-idx.yml schema validation fails because cdefault node is missing in the schema
cause: The cbuild-idx.yml schema did not define the cdefault node that the toolbox writes, and additionalProperties is false, so validation of generated files failed.
fix: Add cdefault to the schema so it matches the current output and stays tolerant of keys from previous versions; agreed as PRs #1416 and #1419 in the 2024-04-02 meeting, no release named.

title: csolution: Local repository packs handled inconsistently by list packs and convert
cause: Local repository packs were added to the pack list without version filtering and ignored when the cbuild-pack requirements were established, so an older installed pack could win over a newer local one.
fix: Fixed in csolution: local packs are visible wherever installed packs are used and take precedence when their version is equal or larger within the requested range. The thread names no release.

title: csolution: Build fails because an optional layer variable such as Shield-Layer is undefined
cause: Layer variables referenced in layers: must be defined; there is no implicit skipping of an optional layer.
fix: Define the variable as an empty string in the target-type (variables: - Shield-Layer: ""); a layer entry with an empty path is ignored. The thread asked that layer detection list this empty variable in the cbuild-idx configurations, which was then reported to work.

title: csolution: Partial component name resolves to an unexpected pack's component
cause: csolution 2.5.0-devint5 resolved the partly specified ARM::CMSIS Driver:USART to its best match ARM::CMSIS Driver:USART:Custom from ARM::CMSIS (Custom is a Csub). The documented rule is that :Csub is not selected for the user; after a later nightly partial identifiers such as CMSIS:OS Tick no longer resolved without their Csub.
fix: Write the full identifier including the Csub where the component has one, for example CMSIS:OS Tick:SysTick, as done for the csolution-examples in PR #41 and other Open-CMSIS-Pack projects.

title: csolution: Two DFP packs resolve the same device name; the cprj lists both DFPs
cause: The device exists with the same Dvendor and Dname in two installed packs (an official and another vendor's DFP), so csolution may select either.
fix: Reduce the pack scope by installing only the relevant packs; the pack selection mechanism (packs: in csolution.yml) was still under development and not accepted by csolution 0.9.2.

title: csolution: Schema check of cbuild files rejects component versions in MAJOR.MINOR form
cause: The rejected *.cbuild.yml had been generated by CMSIS-Toolbox 2.7.0, whose problem was fixed in 2.8.0; it was not a schema defect.
fix: Update to CMSIS-Toolbox 2.8.0 or later so that the cbuild files are generated by the new version.

title: csolution: cbuild-run.yml flash algorithm limited to one processor on multi-core devices
cause: csolution collects device data through the RTE model per Pname of the selected contexts, so it wrote a pname for each algorithm even where the pack gave no Pname, which restricted a shared algorithm to a single core.
fix: Fixed by devtools PR #2039, in CMSIS-Toolbox nightly #435 and later: pname is only written when the pack specifies it.

title: csolution: cbuild-run.yml debug-topology lacks processors not used by the selected context
cause: csolution listed in debug-topology only the processors used by the selected contexts, but pyOCD examines the complete device at connect and needs the full topology; flash algorithms were filtered the same way (#2026).
fix: Fixed by devtools PR #2046, in CMSIS-Toolbox nightly #444 and later: debug-topology lists all processors of the device. Update the toolbox.

title: csolution: cbuild-run.yml output list wrong for dual-core; AC6 .bin is a directory
cause: With fromelf, converting an image with several load regions to --bin creates a directory instead of a single file, so the expected .bin file seems missing. A load: given for a project-context without type: was applied to all generated types, including hex and bin.
fix: PR #2171 makes the project-context load: apply only to the generated ELF and no longer allows type: there. Per the agreed rule, with AC6 and a generated HEX the image should come from the HEX and the symbols from the AXF; the reporter found an explicit load: image+symbols still did not follow it, and the thread ends there.

title: csolution: cbuild-pack.yml contains only an empty resolved-packs entry
cause: The reporter traced the corrupted cbuild-pack.yml (resolved-packs: - {}) to for-context: +AVH* written without escaping the leading plus; the maintainer could not reproduce the problem.
fix: Write the value as \+AVH* in for-context:. The report could no longer be reproduced with nightly CMSIS Solution extension builds, which clean up when switching between target sets.

title: csolution: csolution cannot find cproject.yml when names contain non-ASCII characters on Windows
cause: csolution 2.11.0 on Windows corrupts non-ASCII characters in file names and paths (an encoding issue), so it cannot find the referenced cproject.yml. CMake also restricts the characters of target names, which are formed from project names, target types, build types and execute names.
fix: Workaround: enable the Windows option 'Beta: Use Unicode UTF-8 for worldwide language support' (system-wide, may affect legacy tools). Keep project names, target types, build types and execute names ASCII. A documentation note was requested.

title: csolution: Layer search finds nothing when the project names only a board and no device
cause: Layer detection required device: to be given and did not derive the device from the board's mounted device.
fix: Use the CMSIS-Toolbox nightly (as included in the CMSIS Solution extension of 2026-07-28 or later): the device is derived from the board and the layer selection appears. The pack that holds the layer must still be installed.

title: csolution: GDB call stack loops or never ends with AC6/ATfE code built with debug enabled
cause: AC6 and ATfE optimise functions with the noreturn attribute (threads) so that they use or destroy the link register without emitting the matching debug information (.cfi_undefined 14), which seems to be a compiler issue (not yet confirmed). GDB then cannot stop unwinding the stack.
fix: Compile debug builds with -funwind-tables: the code keeps LR on the stack (slightly more stack) and unwinding works reliably. The issue proposes adding it by default for AC6 and CLANG when debug: on, and #2612 suggests adding it to cdefault.

title: csolution: add-paths ignored or error when used under files or repeated as map keys
cause: add-paths is accepted for a single file, a group, a component, the project, a layer, the solution and build or target types, but not for the files list, and it only affects the sources compiled at that level, so a path given for a group does not reach a component's sources. Repeating the add-paths key in one map is invalid YAML because keys must be unique.
fix: Put the include path where the failing source is compiled: on the component that needs it (e.g. Device:STM32Cube HAL:Common) or at project level, and write several paths as one list (add-paths: [., ./targets/board] or one entry per line).

title: csolution: Generated cprj references a pack version that was not requested for a local pack
cause: The thread gives no analysis: the cprj requested basic_trace 0.1.0 while local_repository.pidx listed 0.0.3, so the build could not find the requested version of the local pack.
fix: The maintainer considered it fixed in CMSIS-Toolbox 1.0.0 (not validated by the reporter); the tools read the version of a local pack from the pdsc file.

title: csolution: IAR linker script .icf is converted to category other and the link fails
cause: The .icf extension was not recognized as a linker script, so the cprj entry got category other.
fix: Fixed in CMSIS-Toolbox 1.5.0, which recognizes .icf as a linker script.

title: csolution: Partly specified component is not resolved using isDefaultVariant of the pack
