cause: csolution first collects the matching components and then picks one, ahead of the RTE model logic that honours isDefaultVariant, so the pack's default variant was ignored. A partly specified component resolves only to a single match (Cversion not considered), and then the highest Cversion is taken.
fix: Give the full component ID including the Cvariant so that it resolves to one match. Respecting isDefaultVariant was announced for CMSIS-Toolbox 2.0.0-dev3; a trailing & to denote an empty Cvariant was proposed.

title: csolution: Files silently missing because for-compiler: appears twice in one group mapping
cause: A YAML mapping with two for-compiler keys is invalid, but the yaml-cpp parser accepts duplicate keys, so csolution's schema check did not report it and the GCC files were silently not included.
fix: Write one group per compiler, or put for-compiler on each file entry; the schema check in VS Code flags the error. Fixed in csolution by PR #1107; the thread names no release.

title: csolution: csolution list configs without a solution file crashes silently
cause: 'csolution list configs' without an input *.csolution.yml crashed silently with a non-zero exit code instead of reporting the missing argument.
fix: Pass the solution file, e.g. csolution list configs <name>.csolution.yml. Nightly builds from 2024-12-02 (csolution 2.6.0+p56) report 'input yml files were not specified' instead of crashing.

title: csolution: cdefault.yml compiler option overrides the same option set in csolution or cproject
cause: The misc options of the different levels are additive and their order on the command line is implementation defined: cproject, then csolution, then cdefault, then build-type, then target-type. Because the last occurrence of a repeated option wins in AC6, Clang and GCC, a value from cdefault.yml (for example -gdwarf4) beats one from csolution.yml (-gdwarf5).
fix: No change yet: a reordering with cdefault first, so that csolution and cproject options override it, was proposed as a breaking change and put up for review. The generated compile_commands.json shows the effective order.

title: csolution: Wrong GCC picked when several GCC toolchains are on PATH
cause: CMake falls back to a gcc from PATH if the compiler is not registered.
fix: Register the compiler with the environment variable GCC_TOOLCHAIN_<major>_<minor>_<patch> holding the absolute path to its bin directory (Toolchain Registration); another user fixed it by correcting the path and environment variables.

message: String does not match the pattern of "(^[A-Za-z\d][\w+()'\/\- \.]+$)|(^([A-Za-z\d][A-Za-z\d ]+::)?
title: csolution: Component ID schema check rejects vendor names with a hyphen (MDK-Packs::)
cause: The regular expression for the component ID in the yml schema did not allow a hyphen in the vendor part; the component itself is valid.
fix: Fixed in the next tools release (duplicate of devtools #805); update the tools.

message: error csolution: board 'ABOV::StarterKit-A31G112CL:V1.1' was not found
title: csolution: board with vendor prefix not found although the pack is installed
cause: csolution 2.5.0 built the board id with the device vendor (Dvendor 'ABOV Semiconductor') instead of the board's vendor 'ABOV', so the board ABOV::StarterKit-A31G112CL:V1.1 was not found.
fix: Use a csolution nightly after 2.5.0, which computes the board id correctly; csolution list boards -f A31G112 then prints ABOV::StarterKit-A31G112CL:V1.1.

message: error csolution: cgen file was not found, run generator 'CubeMX' for context
title: csolution: "cgen file was not found" for CubeMX project built with Arm Compiler
cause: The csolution.yml still set compiler: AC6 while CubeMX was set to generate for the STM32CubeIDE toolchain (GCC).
fix: Make the compiler in csolution.yml match the toolchain selected in CubeMX and run the generator again; the maintainer also asked to check that 'Generate Under Root' was disabled after selecting STM32CubeIDE.

message: error csolution: cmake configuration file and compiler registration environment variable missing, format: GCC_TOOLCHAIN_<major>_<minor>_<patch>
title: csolution: csolution convert aborts when no toolchain environment variable is registered
cause: csolution 2.5.0 enforced a registered toolchain (GCC_TOOLCHAIN_<major>_<minor>_<patch> environment variable) even for csolution convert, which before did not need one; the agreed behaviour is to check it only when cbuild invokes the toolchain.
fix: Fixed (confirmed in the thread, no version named); update csolution. Otherwise register the toolchain via the GCC_TOOLCHAIN_<major>_<minor>_<patch> environment variable.

message: error csolution: context 'gpio-toggle.GCC' was not found
title: csolution: error: context was not found when -c gives only a project or an incomplete context
cause: -c needs the fully qualified context <project>.<build-type>+<target-type>; parts cannot be left out when types exist (it may be omitted only when the solution has a single context).
fix: List the valid names with csolution -s <file> list contexts and pass one in full. A help text saying build-type and target-type are not optional was proposed.

message: error csolution: malformed access sequence: '/$test/Blinky_FRDM-K32L3A6
title: csolution: Project in a directory with a $ in its path fails with malformed access sequence
cause: csolution fails when the absolute output path contains '$', which the reporter suspected collides with access sequences; with output redirected to a path without '$' it succeeds. A maintainer proposed won't fix.
fix: Avoid $ in directory names, or redirect output with -O to a path without it.

message: error csolution: no component was found with identifier 'Keil::Compiler&ARM Compiler:I/O:STDERR&User'
title: csolution: Switching the compiler to GCC gives no component found with identifier errors
cause: Some components listed in the project have toolchain-specific files (for example assembler sources) and are not available for GCC, so csolution cannot resolve them after the compiler is switched; GCC itself is supported by the tools.
fix: Replace or remove the components that are only available for Arm Compiler when building with GCC.

message: error csolution: no component was found with identifier 'Security:mbed TLS'
title: csolution: csolution run -g fails with missing component of an unselected sibling context
cause: All contexts that share the generator id, base-dir and cgen-file (and multi-core, secure/non-secure and map: siblings) are processed together, and a defect did not load packs additionally required by the unselected siblings, causing a false dependency failure.
fix: Workaround: select all sibling contexts, here by leaving out -c, for example csolution run Network.csolution.yml -g CubeMX. csolution list generators <solution> -v shows the siblings.

message: error csolution: no default rwx memory nor algorithm with ramstart/size was found
title: csolution: csolution 2.9.0 stops with "no default rwx memory" for a device pack
cause: The device pack description had many errors reported by packchk (schema errors such as the Dvendor value, the element order in <devices>, unsupported characters in descriptions and an invalid startup attribute on <algorithm>); csolution 2.9.0 reported the error for it while 2.8.0 built the project.
fix: Run packchk on the pack and fix the reported errors in the pdsc; the reporter then said the problem was solved.

message: error csolution: redefinition from 'GCC' into 'AC6' is not allowed
title: csolution: --toolchain GCC conflicts with layer that fixes compiler AC6
cause: In CMSIS-Toolbox 2.5.0, for projects with layers the compiler given with --toolchain GCC was redefined back to AC6 from the yml input, and that redefinition was rejected.
fix: Solved in a CMSIS-Toolbox release after 2.5.0 (an internal release at the time); update the toolbox.

message: error csolution: solution requires newer CMSIS-Toolbox version 2.12.0
title: csolution: Error that the solution requires a newer CMSIS-Toolbox version
cause: The created-for: node of the solution names a minimum CMSIS-Toolbox version that is higher than the version of the CMSIS-Toolbox manifest in use (not the csolution executable version).
fix: Use a CMSIS-Toolbox at least as new as created-for. Newer csolution builds name the file, the required and the current version; the message stays an error on the command line but is a warning in RPC mode (VS Code), where a schema error still stops processing.

message: error csolution: source modules added by multiple components:
title: csolution: Error that source modules are added by multiple components since 2.5.0
cause: Since CMSIS-Toolbox 2.5.0 the default CMake generator (cbuild2cmake) builds per component, so the same source file listed by two components would give multiple objects with the same symbols at link time. The check is intended; in cbuildgen mode it is only a warning.
fix: Fix the pack so the file belongs to one component. Short term: run cbuild with --cbuildgen, or pin the toolbox to 2.4.0 in vcpkg-configuration.json (the CMSIS Solution Build button cannot pass --cbuildgen). The maintainers announced that duplicated files would be hidden from subsequent components.

message: missing properties: 'from-pack'
title: csolution: Schema 2.3 rejects cbuild.yml files written by toolbox 2.1/2.2 (from-pack missing)
cause: Schema version 2.3 made from-pack required for generators, but cbuild.yml files written by cbuild 2.1/2.2 do not contain it, so validating them with that schema fails.
fix: Remove from-pack from the required list of the generator entry so it is optional (the reporter patched the schema this way); the maintainers agreed to make this change, but the thread shows no release with it.

message: provided combined connections not consumed:
title: csolution: Layer rejected because the project provides a connection that no layer consumes
cause: The rule that a layer is unused when none of its provided connections are consumed was also applied to the project itself, so a project whose provides: entry had no consumer was skipped in layer detection.
fix: The implementation was changed so a project stays valid even if none of its provided connections are consumed; the rule remains for layers. The thread names no release with the change.

message: warning csolution: context 'Project.Debug+SSE-310-MPS3_FVP': required pack 'ARM::CMSIS-Compiler@2.0.0' is not loaded
title: csolution: Warning that a required pack is not loaded or not specified
cause: A pack in use (for example a BSP) lists other packs under requirements in its pdsc; csolution warns when those are not part of the pack selection, as a hint where an unresolved component or dependency could come from.
fix: Informational: add the named pack to packs: when a component or dependency is not resolved. The message was reworded (PR #1364) to name the pack that requires it.

message: warning csolution: key 'selected-by' was not recognized
title: csolution: Warning that key 'selected-by' was not recognized in cbuild-pack.yml
cause: The cbuild-pack.yml was written by an older toolbox (2.2) that used selected-by, later renamed selected-by-pack.
fix: Fixed in CMSIS-Toolbox 2.3.0, which copes with both keys.

message: warning: (Error: pc 0x8020a6d8 in address map, but not in symtab.)
title: GDB: GDB warnings "pc ... in read in CU, but not in symtab" with Arm Compiler images
cause: The warnings come from GDB with AC6-built images and showed with RTOS views enabled. A maintainer's tentative reading: the AC6 debug info looks sensible, but GDB treats every address in a CU's .debug_addr table as a code address, including const data placed in code sections, and a cross-check against the symbol table then fails.
fix: The warnings are harmless. Discarding them from the Debug Console through the CMSIS Debugger debug tracker was proposed and is addressed in PR #688 (no release named); GDB used from the command line outside VS Code still shows them.

message: /home/postCreateCommand.sh: line 12: vcpkg: command not found
title: other: Devcontainer postCreate fails with "vcpkg: command not found"
cause: vcpkg changed its activation command: 'vcpkg activate' no longer works and 'vcpkg-shell activate' takes its place, so the postCreate script fails.
fix: Call vcpkg-shell activate in the postCreate script (proposed in PR #262). Separately, the devcontainer build can fail when the .armlm or .iarlm folders mounted by devcontainer.json do not exist; creating them was suggested by the reporter.

message: fatal error: filesystem: No such file or directory
title: other: Building devtools fails with fatal error: filesystem: No such file or directory
cause: The sources use std::filesystem, which needs GCC 8 or newer; GCC 7.5 does not provide the header.
fix: Build with GCC 8 or later (a README change, PR #27, was proposed to state this).

title: packchk: packchk does not warn about missing Cvariant components referenced in accept
cause: The RTE model only reports a missing component (M504) for require expressions; components named only in accept conditions were not checked, so a missing variant went unnoticed.
fix: As a check, temporarily change accept to require to see M504 messages for missing components. The maintainers planned to extend packchk to check all references; the thread ends with a request for a test version, no release.

message:
*** ERROR M218:
  Unable to find PACK.xsd schema file. Searched in './, ../etc/, ../../etc/' relative to '<path>'.
title: packchk: packchk printed nothing when PACK.xsd could not be found
cause: packchk looks for the schema in ./, ../etc/ and ../../etc/ relative to the executable and used to stay silent when it was absent.
fix: Place PACK.xsd in one of those folders or pass --xsd <file>. From packchk 1.4.0 error M218 names the searched folders; a later development build words it with the executable path and adds M219 for a --xsd file that is not found.

message:
*** ERROR M310: <pack>.pdsc (Line 597)
  Filename mismatch (case sensitive):
title: packchk: ERROR M310 Filename mismatch for pdsc paths that begin with a dot (.config/...)
cause: The case-sensitivity check trims leading ./ characters with find_first_not_of, which also strips the dot of a hidden folder name.
fix: For the time being use the PackChk binary from CMSIS_5 (develop branch, CMSIS/Utilities); the maintainer named the code fix (use find("./") instead), no release is shown.

message:
*** WARNING M339: <pack>.pdsc (Line 631)
  Include Path 'Inc' must not be a file!
title: packchk: WARNING M339 Include Path must not be a file for an existing folder
cause: The directory test was inverted when the check was ported to RteFsUtils.
fix: Fixed and verified with #123; in the meantime use the PackChk binary from the CMSIS_5 develop branch (CMSIS/Utilities). The thread names no release.

message: Aborted
title: packchk: packchk from CMSIS-Toolbox 2.0.0 aborts on Ubuntu 20.04
cause: The schema validation uses the Xerces library, which converts input through iconv; that library changed in glibc between Ubuntu 20.04 and 22.04, so the packchk binary crashes on Ubuntu 20.04.
fix: Run packchk with --disable-validation, which skips the Xerces schema check and lets the remaining checks run. A packchk build on Ubuntu 20.04 was planned, but the issue was rejected because this workaround exists.

message: Not Semantic Versioning: '2.0.0-alpha.0.5'
title: packchk: M394 Not Semantic Versioning for pre-release versions with dots (2.0.0-alpha.0.5)
cause: packchk's own version parser did not accept dot-separated pre-release identifiers, which SemVer allows; error M394 cannot be suppressed with -x.
fix: The maintainer was changing packchk to check versions with the PackVersionType regular expression of PACK.xsd; the thread does not confirm a merged fix or a release.

message: attempted static link of dynamic object libcurl.so
title: packchk: Building packchk on Linux fails: attempted static link of dynamic object libcurl.so
cause: Xerces-C picks up libcurl when it is installed, but packchk is linked with -static and libcurl.so cannot be linked statically.
fix: Build Xerces with its option network=OFF; packchk is agreed to need no network support.

title: pyOCD: pyOCD 0.45.0 skips flash algorithm when its RAM address is not a declared memory region
cause: pyOCD 0.45.0 rejects a flash algorithm whose RAMstart lies outside every explicit RAM region of the pack description. The algorithm is dropped and the flash region ends up without a flash instance, although the address is valid RAM on the device.
fix: Use a pyOCD with pyOCD PR 2012, tested in a CMSIS Debugger nightly build, where programming the M55M1 worked again.

title: pyOCD: Unreliable flash programming on STM32H7 (hard fault after load)
cause: Double-buffered downloads stall on buses with strict timing.
fix: Use a pyOCD with double buffering disabled by default, first provided in the standalone pyOCD build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild2.

title: pyOCD: CoreSight root components on APv2 are read from wrong addresses
cause: ap_address was passed to the memory interface for root components.
fix: Use a pyOCD that no longer passes ap_address when it creates root components, first provided in the standalone pyOCD build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild4.

title: pyOCD: Flash programming fails on LPC55S69 when the device is erased
cause: Before programming, pyOCD reads flash to compare it with the image; on an erased LPC55S69 these direct reads cause bus errors.
fix: Use a pyOCD that skips reading erased sectors when the flash algorithm provides a Verify function, first in the standalone build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild4.

title: pyOCD: Attach again to the same core fails after detaching
cause: pyOCD gdbserver exits after the client disconnects unless --persist is given.
fix: Add --persist to the pyOCD gdbserver arguments; the maintainers planned to add it to the launch and tasks templates.

title: pyOCD: monitor reset leaves GUI out of sync; use monitor reset halt
cause: pyOCD monitor commands change the CPU state without GDB async records, so the GUI does not learn about running or stopped.
fix: Use 'monitor reset halt' instead of 'monitor reset', or configure the reset button with resetDeviceCommands such as 'monitor reset halt hardware'; a single step afterwards brings the GUI back in sync.

title: pyOCD: Symbol file paths in cbuild-run are relative to the file, which moved to the out folder
cause: Paths in the cbuild-run file are relative to that file, and pyOCD did not resolve them that way; this breaks once CMSIS-Toolbox 2.11 places the cbuild-run file in the out directory.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with PR 1788 (validated with a local build together with a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly; no release named).

title: pyOCD: GD-Link (CMSIS-DAP v1 without serial number) not found by pyOCD 0.38 / extension 1.0.0
cause: A regression in pyOCD's hidapi backend broke CMSIS-DAP v1 probes that report no USB serial number, such as the GD-Link, although 'pyocd list' shows the probe; extension 0.5.0 still worked.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with the hidapi fix from the CMSIS Debugger team (the reporter verified a test build). To try a custom pyOCD in the extension, change its path in launch.json and in every pyocd entry of tasks.json.

title: pyOCD: HE core on Alif E7 does not start after flashing
cause: pyOCD did not apply a hardware reset after flashing; the maintainers expected the missing clean post-load state to be why the HE core did not start.
fix: Use pyOCD 0.40 / CMSIS Debugger 1.2.0 or later (reset catch on all cores, no implicit resets between images, hardware reset after flashing).

title: pyOCD: CMSIS-DAP v1 probe initialisation fails because of wrong HID report size handling
cause: pyOCD used incorrect HID report sizes with some CMSIS-DAP v1 probes.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with PR 1854 (merged into develop; confirmed on Windows and macOS with workflow artifacts, no release named). Linux does not use the hidapi backend and still failed for one reporter.

title: pyOCD: Internal pyOCD targets fail to program after double buffering was disabled
cause: After double buffering was disabled by default, the flash algorithms of some pyOCD internal targets used a different buffer address, so programming failed.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with PR 1898: double buffering is enabled again by default for internal targets, begin_data is replaced by a single page_buffers entry, and STM32H7xx internal targets keep only one buffer. It was tested on several boards; no release is named.

title: pyOCD: pyOCD discovery stops with a critical error when a core AP has no pname in the pack
cause: A core access point discovered during CoreSight discovery (a hidden core) had no matching pname entry in the PDSC, and the mapping step raised instead of ignoring it.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with PR 1865 (validated by the original reporter, merged into the develop branch; no release named). The earlier PR 1801 covered only the internal pack support, not cbuild-run targets.

title: pyOCD: pyOCD internal pack support fails when an algorithm path contains ".."
cause: The flash algorithm path from the PDSC was used without normalization, so paths such as Pack/../other/Flash/x.FLM could not be opened.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with PR 1867, which was merged into the develop branch; no release is named.

title: pyOCD: RTT broken on single-core devices when control block is found by ELF symbol
cause: pyOCD handled the pname of a single-core target wrongly, so the lookup of the RTT control block by its ELF symbol failed.
fix: Update to pyOCD 0.43.1 / CMSIS Debugger 1.4.1 or later, which contain pyOCD PR #1923.

title: pyOCD: pyocd load exits 1 after a good flash because the post-load reset drops the connection
cause: The default post-load reset for cbuild-run targets is a hardware reset. With the default ResetHardware sequence the debug connection can be lost right after it, the board uninit steps then fail, and load exits non-zero although programming worked; the CMSIS Load pre-launch task then shows an error pop-up.
fix: Use a pyOCD with PR 1971: a hardware post-load reset runs after board uninit, and for other reset types failures are reported as information with exit code 0 when flashing succeeded.

title: pyOCD: Probe shows up under a wrong board name after changing the DAP serial string
cause: pyOCD maps probe serial-number prefixes to Mbed board IDs, and a bug in the CMSIS-DAP board identification code matched the custom serial string to a u-blox board.
fix: Fixed via change #1090. Board ID background is documented on the pyOCD wiki page 'Board IDs'.

title: pyOCD: Flashing a blank LPC5526 fails with a memory transfer fault
cause: LPC5526 had no built-in pyOCD target, unlike the LPC55S28 whose target uses the LPC5500 family code (which carries a comment the reporter suspected matches this case); flashing a blank part failed with a memory transfer fault while erase always worked.
fix: Add a built-in target for the LPC5526 like the LPC55S28 one; the reporter did this and could then flash, erase and debug.

title: pyOCD: STM32L475 built-in target has wrong DBGMCU register addresses
cause: The built-in STM32L475 target had wrong addresses for the DBGMCU APB1FZR2 and APB2FZR freeze registers.
fix: Fixed by change #1193. For other STM32 parts (e.g. L496) use the CMSIS pack target and write DBGMCU registers from a user script (did_connect hook); debug sequence support was only on the maintainer's feature/debug_sequences branch.

title: pyOCD: new micro:bit V2 fails to flash with chip or sector erase until mass erase
cause: The thread gives no confirmed cause. The reporter suspected that new micro:bit V2 units have access-port protection enabled, which only a mass erase (ERASEALL) clears; the micro:bit side said the flash is not locked on purpose. The failure also came back after flashing the out-of-box hex or a hex from the online editor.
fix: Once: pyocd erase --mass -t nrf52833, then flash as usual. Dragging the file to the micro:bit drive (MSD) first also works.

title: pyOCD: PSoC 5LP kit with KitProg v1 is not detected
cause: The CY8CKIT-059 has KitProg (v1), which has no CMSIS-DAP mode; pyOCD supports only KitProg2 in CMSIS-DAP mode and KitProg3. PSoC 5LP devices are not really supported by pyOCD either (no CMSIS-Pack, no flash programming).
fix: No fix for this kit in pyOCD; only KitProg2 (switched to CMSIS-DAP mode with its button) or KitProg3 probes are detected.

title: pyOCD: -f frequency option ignored with ST-Link V3
cause: A copy-and-paste bug kept pyOCD from applying the requested SWD frequency to an ST-Link V3. After the fix the measured clock still differs from the request because of how the ST-Link V3 derives its frequencies, the same as in Keil MDK.
fix: Use a pyOCD with the fix, first available on the develop branch (pip install from git @develop); a new stlink.v3_prescaler option selects the probe's prescaler.

title: pyOCD: Renesas RA pack: flash algorithm not found, target type not recognized
cause: The Renesas pack stores its pdsc in a subdirectory; pyOCD found the pdsc but resolved the algorithm paths relative to the archive root.
fix: pyOCD was to be changed to accept this non-standard layout (PR #1461); use a pyOCD that includes it.

title: pyOCD: gdb 'load' fails on a custom W7500 target until the flash analyzer is enabled
cause: The new W7500 target's flash algorithm definition had analyzer_supported off and a begin_data RAM address that did not work, so gdb 'load' failed.
fix: In the target's flash algorithm definition set analyzer_supported to true and begin_data to a usable RAM address (0x20002000 on the W7500).

title: pyOCD: write_memory to STM32G0 option bytes address has no effect
cause: STM32 option bytes live in flash and are protected by lock registers. A plain memory write to 0x1FFF7800 is ignored. The option bytes are loaded from flash into FLASH_OPTR and related registers at power-on and only rewritten through the flash controller.
fix: Program them through the flash controller. The maintainer suggested pyOCD's flash classes (MemoryLoader.program_binary_data, or MemoryLoader.add_data and commit); the user got it working with the reference-manual sequence: unlock FLASH_KEYR then FLASH_OPTKEYR, write the new value to FLASH_OPTR, start the update in FLASH_CR, and expect a reset from OBL_LAUNCH. An exception is raised and the session object is unusable afterwards, so create a new one. With firmware already in the chip the first FLASH_KEYR write raised a transfer fault until a chip erase was done.

title: pyOCD: pack target crashes at session init on multi-AP Cortex-M33 devices like EFR32BG22/24
cause: The error log in the thread is cut off before the failure. A suggested patch points at pack_target.py, where each discovered core's AP address is looked up in the pack's processors_ap_map; on these multi-AP Cortex-M33 devices that lookup can fail for a core whose AP is not in the map. The maintainer said it should be fixed by #1865.
fix: Create a built-in target from the pack's flash algorithm (docs/adding_new_targets.md), which made 0.36.0 work with an EFR32BG24. Skipping cores whose AP address is missing from processors_ap_map in pack_target.py was suggested, but did not solve it for the reporter. #1865 was named as the fix.

title: pyOCD: STM32H7 flash corrupted occasionally with double buffering
cause: Double-buffered flash programming can stall on the bus of devices with strict timing such as STM32H7, leaving pages partly written (rest 0xFF) without any error.
fix: Upgrade to a current pyOCD (v0.38.0 when the issue was closed), which disables double buffering for flash algorithms by default. A built-in stm32h743xx target adapted to the H750 flash layout also programmed reliably, unlike the pack's flash loader.

title: pyOCD: External nRF51 board cannot be flashed through an nRF51-DK running mbed interface firmware
cause: The CMSIS-DAP firmware only drives the SWD pins to the on-board nRF51; the Debug Out header is not used.
fix: No fix in the thread: the CMSIS-DAP firmware would have to detect an external target and switch SWD to Debug Out, and the reporter planned a feature request for it. With the J-Link firmware the external board could be programmed before.

title: pyOCD: DAP TransferError when flashing a K64F with blank flash
cause: The error occurs when the K64F's flash has been erased and left blank.
fix: Suggested workaround: load another image over the mass-storage interface to recover the device. The maintainer later said that problems with blank flash on Kinetis devices should all be fixed, without naming a release.

title: pyOCD: pyOCD 0.12 install pulls enum34 on Python 3.4+ and breaks the standard library
cause: The requirements listed enum34 unconditionally. Installed on Python 3.4 or newer it overrides the standard enum module and breaks parts of the standard library, such as IntFlag.
fix: Install pyOCD 0.12.1, which backports the setup.py fix that restricts enum34 to Python below 3.4.

title: pyOCD: STLink probe appears and disappears with 'The device has no langid' on Windows
cause: On Windows, STLink discovery through the custom USB match function intermittently failed to read the STLink's USB device fields ('The device has no langid'), so the probe list alternated between found and empty.
fix: Use a pyOCD version with the maintainer's permanent fix, which the reporter confirmed (no release named). The reporter's workaround was to find the STLink by VID 0x0483 / PID 0x374b in get_all_connected_devices instead of the custom match.

title: pyOCD: Config file not named pyocd.yaml is ignored, target stays generic cortex_m
cause: The target override and test_binary options were placed in a file called test_boards.yaml. pyOCD reads its config from pyocd.yaml (the functional tests switched to that name), so the target stayed at the generic cortex_m type, which has no flash support or memory map.
fix: Rename the file to pyocd.yaml and set target_override and test_binary there (or pass --target), then check the 'Target type is ...' log line to confirm the target.

title: pyOCD: gdb and SWV together on a CMSIS-DAP probe corrupt each other's responses
cause: The SWO polling thread (DAP_SWO_Data) and the transfer thread used the same probe endpoint without synchronisation, so their DAP responses were mixed up on probes without a separate SWO streaming endpoint.
fix: The maintainer reported it fixed; the thread names no version or change.

title: pyOCD: Erase or flash of LPC55S28 hits an assertion because the core is never halted
cause: The LPC55xx boot ROM needs custom handling to halt after reset; the LPC552x had no built-in target so that logic was not used, and the -t lpc55s69 workaround fails because the LPC552x is single-core while the LPC55S69 target assumes two cores.
fix: Use pyOCD with the later changes: the single-core handling of PR #884 resolved the halt failure, and #885 added LPC55S28 support with an updated flash algorithm. The reporter still saw a chip-erase hang with the development head.

title: pyOCD: Flashing an nRF52 via ST-LINK V2 fails with 'STLink error (29)' after a tool update
cause: ST-Link firmware V2J37S7 apparently refuses to work with non-STM32 devices (the maintainer's belief); with V2J34S7 the nRF52832 could be flashed again.
fix: Downgrade the ST-Link firmware to an older version such as V2J34S7.

title: pyOCD: pyocd from a distribution package (Arch AUR) fails with an import traceback at start
cause: The Arch AUR package did not install python-future, which pylink-square (a pyOCD dependency) requires and which pip would have installed.
fix: Install the missing python-future package, or install pyOCD with pip (e.g. in an isolated environment); report it to the distribution package maintainer.

title: pyOCD: Writing a single UICR word after flashing with the API leaves an nRF52 unbootable
cause: The user suspected that the FlashLoader (chip_erase='sector', smart_flash=True) erased more flash than intended for the small UICR write; the same write done with write16 in commander left a bootable device.
fix: After FileProgrammer has loaded the image, program the extra bytes with the low-level Flash class: create Flash(target, boot_memory.algo), set flasher.region to the boot memory region, call init(operation=Flash.Operation.PROGRAM), then program_phrase(address, bytes), and reset the target.

title: pyOCD: Listing probes and installed packs from the pyOCD Python API
cause: pyocd list and pyocd pack show are built on Python helpers that a program can call directly.
fix: Use pyocd.core.helpers.ConnectHelper.get_all_connected_probes(blocking=False) to get probe objects with product_name and unique_id, and pyocd.target.pack.pack_target.ManagedPacks.get_installed_packs() for the installed packs (vendor, pack, version, pack file).

message: 'SYS_AP_PSoC64' object has no attribute 'core'
title: pyOCD: Session open fails: 'SYS_AP_PSoC64' object has no attribute 'core'
cause: GenericMemAPTarget inherits from CoreSightComponent instead of CoreSightCoreComponent (as it did in 0.32.3), so DebugContext's isinstance check fails when a session is opened.
fix: The maintainer said pull request #1350 should fix it; not confirmed in the thread.

message: 0000350:ERROR:__main__:uncaught exception: argument should be integer or bytes-like object, not 'str'
title: pyOCD: pyocd list crashes on macOS when hidapi returns the product name as bytes
cause: On macOS with Python 3, hid.enumerate() can return the product string as bytes, and the CMSIS-DAP name check in hidapi_backend.py searched it with a str.
fix: Convert the product string to str before searching for 'CMSIS-DAP' in hidapi_backend.py, as the reporter did and proposed in PR #526.

message: 0000387:ERROR:__main__:uncaught exception: 'utf16' codec can't decode byte 0x6c in position 30: truncated data
title: pyOCD: pyocd list -p crashes with a utf16 decode error on old ST-Link firmware
cause: ST-Link firmware older than V2J28 reports a USB interface name truncated to an odd number of bytes, which pyusb cannot decode as UTF-16.
fix: Use pyOCD with change #616, which the reporter confirmed fixes it; ST-Link firmware V2J28 or later does not trigger the crash.

message: 0000421:CRITICAL:__main__:No cores were discovered!
title: pyOCD: STM32F7 (F746) 'No cores were discovered' in Mbed Studio
cause: STM32F7 and H7 parts need special handling to wake from low-power modes before discovery; the F746 target lacked it, while the F767 target had the DBGMCU handling.
fix: Use a pyocd with the F767 support (master at the time) and select -t stm32f767zi on an F746 (worked for one user; it only reports a dual-bank error and continues). Use debug builds that do not sleep, or set DBGMCU_CR early in firmware. Be careful with dual-bank option bytes (nDBANK=0): sector erase may then erase too little; use chip erase or switch to single bank.

message: 0000506:ERROR:__main__:uncaught exception: The device has no langid
title: pyOCD: pyocd gdbserver aborts with 'The device has no langid' when an Android phone is attached
cause: While scanning USB devices, pyOCD's pyusb backend read the interface name strings of every device; an Android phone without a language ID made pyusb raise ValueError, which aborted the probe scan (likely a regression from PR #595).
fix: Use a pyOCD with the workaround from PR #616 (verified on master), or unplug the other device.

message: 0000721:CRITICAL:__main__:No cores were discovered!
title: pyOCD: STM32H743 'No cores were discovered' in Mbed Studio
cause: STM32H7 needs the DBGMCU CR bits set (TRACECLKEN, D1DBGCKEN, D3DBGCKEN and the DBGSLEEP/STOP/STBY bits) for CoreSight discovery to work.
fix: Suggested by the maintainer, not confirmed in the thread: use a pyocd user script that writes DBGMCU_CR, or set the bits at the start of your firmware and load the first image by drag and drop. A branch with CMSIS-Pack debug sequences configured it automatically. Mbed Studio's bundled pyocd is customised, so also ask that team.

message: 0000732 C Invalid .cbuild-run.yml file '<project>/out/App/App.cbuild.yml' [__main__]
title: pyOCD: pyocd load says "Invalid .cbuild-run.yml file" when given a .cbuild.yml file
cause: The --cbuild-run option was pointed at the cbuild.yml build description instead of the generated *.cbuild-run.yml, and the message did not say what was wrong.
fix: Pass the file ending in .cbuild-run.yml. A clearer error message was implemented in pyOCD PR 2003; no release is named.

message: 0000735 C STLink error (66): Unknown command [__main__]
title: pyOCD: Connect mode pre-reset fails with ST-Link probes
cause: In pre-reset mode pyOCD ran its post-reset recovery on a device that was not yet connected, which the ST-Link rejects.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with PR 2036; the thread names no release.

message: 0000954 C Error: <APv1Address@0x1a968104350 #1 dp=0> [__main__]
title: pyOCD: Warning "invalid control node" and then connect crash on multi-core Infineon T2G
cause: pyOCD's native processing of pack debug sequences did not handle a control node without if or while and skipped it with a warning. With cbuild-run debug sequences, the multi-core device then failed because its debug topology was not described in the cbuild-run file.
fix: Use the pyOCD of the CMSIS Debugger v0.0.3 pre-release or later, which takes debug sequences from the cbuild-run file. For the multi-core device, describe debug ports, access ports and processors in the cbuild-run file: proper support was expected with CMSIS-Toolbox 2.9.0 and an updated extension, and meanwhile the reporter got it working by adding the preliminary 'debug:' section (debugports with apid and index per access port, processors with pname and apid) by hand.

message: 0001425 W STLink, CMSIS-DAPv2 and PicoProbe probes are not supported because no libusb library was found. [common]
title: pyOCD: pyOCD without libusb on macOS cannot connect to CMSIS-DAPv2 probes
cause: The bundled pyOCD did not contain libusb, so probes that need it (such as ULINKplus with firmware v2) could not connect on macOS; HID probes were not affected.
fix: Use a CMSIS Debugger version with the change from #124, after which macOS users could connect; the thread names no release.

message: 0001483 C Error: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer [__main__]
title: pyOCD: pyOCD gdbserver TypeError after adding an extra access port to debug-topology
cause: Adding a further access port (for example an APB-AP for the debug/trace subsystem) to the debug-topology of a cbuild-run file made pyOCD gdbserver stop with a TypeError while opening its listening socket, because the port it tried to bind was None. The problem affects ADIv5 and ADIv6 devices.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with PR 1965 (confirmed with a manually triggered pyOCD nightly build; no release named). On ADIv5 devices the extra access port can be reached instead by setting __ap to its index in the debug sequences; ADIv6 needs the apid declared in the debug-topology.

message: 0001679 C RW section does not follow RO section [__main__]
title: pyOCD: GDB server exits with "RW section does not follow RO section"
cause: pyOCD checked the flash algorithm layout too strictly and ignored section alignment.
fix: Use a pyOCD with PR 1795; the maintainers pointed to the CMSIS Debugger pre-release v1.0.0-pre0 for validation, without a result in the thread.

message: 0001754 E Error reading from RTT channel worker 1: SWD/JTAG communication failure (WAIT ACK) [rtt_server]
title: pyOCD: pyOCD run prints RTT SWD/JTAG WAIT ACK errors although the test passes (Alif E8)
cause: pyOCD reads the RTT buffers continuously. On Alif E8 SWD/JTAG WAIT errors tend to occur sporadically just after the target is reset and starts running, also influenced by the processor stubs programmed with the Alif SE tools; a failed iteration is dropped and RTT processing continues.
fix: A single error after reset or a few sporadic ones are usually not critical and only lower the RTT bandwidth (SystemView data can overflow); persistent errors mean RTT no longer works and point to the target or the debug link. The maintainers planned to check whether pyocd run can report it as a warning.

message: 0002270:CRITICAL:__main__:STLink error (9): Get IDCODE error
title: pyOCD: STM32WB55 Nucleo: 'STLink error (9): Get IDCODE error'
cause: The maintainer said a failure to read IDCODE usually means the target is not powered or is in a deep sleep mode; this was not confirmed for this board.
fix: Suggested, not confirmed: use a debug build that does not put the device to sleep, or connect with -Oconnect_mode=under-reset (or set connect_mode in a config file). Use the combined pyocd tool rather than the deprecated pyocd-gdbserver.

message: 0002477 W Zephyr kernel detected. Build your Zephyr application with `CONFIG_DEBUG_THREAD_INFO=y` to enable thread awareness. [zephyr]
title: pyOCD: "Zephyr kernel detected" warning when debugging bare metal
cause: A change on pyOCD's main branch, newer than the last pip release, made the shipped pyOCD warn about a Zephyr kernel for bare-metal applications; with another RTOS such as RTX5 the warning did not appear.
fix: Use a pyOCD from the standalone build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild3 or later, which addresses it.

message: 0009003 C flash erase sector sequence not available (address 0x0804a000) [__main__]
title: pyOCD: pyocd load: "flash erase sector sequence not available" with flashinfo plus FLM in DFP
cause: The generated cbuild-run file contains both a programming algorithm and a flash-info block for the same region. pyOCD 0.44 and later prefers the flash-info block and selects the debug-sequence flash backend, but stm32c5xx_dfp 2.0.0 defines no flash debug sequences, so programming aborts although a working FLM is present.
fix: Use a pyOCD that falls back to the algorithm when no flash sequences exist: it is in the CMSIS Debugger nightly of 2026-06-16, and the maintainers said the next pyOCD release works with the existing DFP. Older workaround: delete the flash-info block from the cbuild-run file. Whether a pack may declare flashinfo without flash sequences was disputed; the specification is to be clarified.

title: pyOCD: Load fails with an empty critical error at 10 MHz debug clock on Alif E7 with ULINKplus
cause: The Alif E7 needs extra time for memory requests, so SWD/JTAG answers WAIT, and pyOCD gave up after too few retries; a lower clock only lengthened the communication so that fewer retries were needed. Programming through the HP core still needed more than 100 retries.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with more WAIT retries (PR 1806: 100, later raised to 150) and the clearer SWD/JTAG error messages of PR 1804; no release is named. Workaround: reduce the debug clock to 5 MHz.

message: 0019032 C Error:  [__main__]
title: pyOCD: Unclear errors "No ACK received" and empty "Error:" when probe or target is missing
cause: pyOCD printed bare SWD/JTAG status for typical wiring or clock problems.
fix: Use a pyOCD with PR 1804 and the follow-up commit that adds the hint to the unexpected-ACK case: messages read like 'SWD/JTAG communication failure (No ACK received); check USB cable, reduce debugger clock'. Check the USB cable and lower the debug clock. A probe connected while pyOCD waits for it is now picked up.

message: 0100505 C Error: already open [__main__]
title: pyOCD: CMSIS-DAP v1 (HID) probes fail on macOS with "already open"
cause: On macOS, opening a CMSIS-DAP v1 (HID) probe timed out, which the reporter put down to a non-working USB connection and a suspected general libusb problem on macOS; the next open attempt then failed with 'already open'.
fix: Use a pyOCD build with PR 1792 (tested with a separate build; no release named).

message: AssertionError
title: pyOCD: pyocd-gdbserver AssertionError at start because another program holds the probe
cause: pyOCD's pywinusb backend timed out opening the probe and hit an assert, which the maintainers read as another process (not pyOCD, which opens the probe exclusively) holding the board.
fix: Not confirmed in the thread: find and close the other program that has the board open, then start pyocd-gdbserver again.

message: AssertionError
title: pyOCD: pyocd-gdbserver raises AssertionError on K64F when run under Python 3
cause: pyOCD did not yet support Python 3, and the reporter ran it under Python 3.6, so target initialisation failed with an AssertionError.
fix: Run pyOCD with Python 2.7, as the maintainer advised; the reporter had switched to OpenOCD instead.

message: Building wheel for hidapi (pyproject.toml) ... error
title: pyOCD: pip install pyocd fails building hidapi on Python 3.14
cause: hidapi had no wheel for Python 3.14 so pip compiled it and needed a C++ build toolchain; libusb-package also lacked a 3.14 wheel at first.
fix: Install again now that hidapi 0.15.0 and a newer libusb-package ship Python 3.14 wheels, so pip no longer has to compile hidapi.

message: C Control block not found [__main__]
title: pyOCD: RTT control block not found when its ID string straddles a 32-byte boundary
cause: pyOCD's RTT control block search failed when the control block ID string crossed a 32-byte boundary.
fix: Workaround: shift the search start by 16 bytes (one of -a 0x20000000 or -a 0x20000010 works) or align the control block to 16 bytes. The fix (#1669) is merged into pyOCD's develop branch.

message: C Error: 'MemoryRange' object has no attribute 'data' [__main__]
title: pyOCD: pyOCD load crashes on flash algorithms without an RW section
cause: pyOCD assumed every flash algorithm has an RW section and failed on a missing section object.
fix: Use a CMSIS Debugger nightly build whose pyOCD skips absent flash algorithm sections (confirmed by the user); no release is named.

message: C Error: <APv1Address@0x1d6da825540 #1 dp=0> [__main__]
title: pyOCD: Connect fails on devices with an extra core not described in the debug topology
cause: Discovery found a second core (the HSM's Cortex-M0+ on AP #1) that the pack's debug topology does not list, and the pack target's lookup of that AP in processors_ap_map raised a KeyError during session open.
fix: Use a pyOCD version containing #1865, which the maintainers said fixes it. They then planned to change it so cores missing from the debug topology are not added to the core list but stay reachable through direct AP access.

message: C Error: Operation not supported or unimplemented on this platform [__main__]
title: pyOCD: -Ocmsis_dap.prefer_v1 ignored by load/gdbserver; v2 open fails on Windows
cause: Probe enumeration reads cmsis_dap.prefer_v1 before command-line options are parsed, so it is ignored. The underlying v2 failure was a libusb bug: interface numbers of 10 or higher are mis-parsed on Windows.
fix: Give the probe's CMSIS-DAP v2 interface a number below 10 (the reporter planned to reorder the USB interfaces), or replace the libusb DLL in the installed libusb-package with a fixed build. The -O cmsis_dap.prefer_v1 option will not take effect for load or gdbserver until sessions are restructured.

message: C No cores were discovered! [__main__]
title: pyOCD: i.MX RT685 pack: debug sequence parse error on 'U' integer suffix and no cores discovered
cause: The NXP pack uses C-style 'U' suffixes on integer literals in a debug sequence, which pyOCD's parser rejected. After that, DebugPortStart was assigned to the named core cm33; pyOCD did not support core-specific DebugPort* sequences, so the debug unlock sequence did not run and the CM33 access port stayed disabled.
fix: Parser fix in pull request #1548 (installable from the branch). For the second problem remove Pname="cm33" from the DebugPortStart sequence in the pdsc and pass the expanded pack directory to --pack, until core-specific port sequences are supported. Use the .FLM extracted from the pack, not NXP's .cfx.

message: C target was not halted as expected after calling flash algorithm routine (IPSR=3) [__main__]
title: pyOCD: HC32F460 flash fails with IPSR=3 after 0.35: wrong target name used with the pack
cause: Not confirmed by the reporter: a contributor who could not reproduce it with the built-in target hc32f460xe on 0.35.1 said the failure seems to come from using the pack part name hc32f460jeua instead of the built-in names hc32f460xc or hc32f460xe. The maintainer noted that 0.35 moved the flash algorithm to the end of RAM, and that 0.34 may not have programmed at all because smart flash skipped unchanged contents.
fix: Try -t hc32f460xe (or hc32f460xc) instead of the pack part name; when comparing versions, pass -Osmart_flash=0 to force programming.

message: C target was not halted as expected after calling flash algorithm routine (IPSR=3) [__main__]
title: pyOCD: Erase/load fails with IPSR=3 after upgrading to 0.36 on Cortex-M0 devices
cause: The flash algorithm was started with the Thumb bit clear in xPSR, which faults on Cortex-M.
fix: Fixed in 0.37.0 by writing the Thumb bit before running algorithm functions; upgrade.

message: CRITICAL:__main__:No ACK received
title: pyOCD: 'No ACK received' on the first access to an nRF52840 board
cause: No response at all to the first SWD read; the maintainer says this most often means the MCU is asleep in a low-power mode (WFI/WFE) that disables debug, and the default Mbed build neither enables debug nor disables sleep on idle.
fix: Build with the Mbed debug profile so debug stays enabled and automatic sleep is off. --connect=under-reset did not help because the nRF52840 does not expose nRESET on a pin unless UICR.PSELRESET is programmed; otherwise try to connect while the firmware is awake or as the MCU powers on.

message: CRITICAL:__main__:No backend available
title: pyOCD: pyocd list fails with 'No backend available' when libusb is missing
cause: The Picoprobe probe class raised NoBackendError while enumerating probes when no libusb backend was installed, instead of just reporting no probes.
fix: Fixed by PR #1128, which the maintainer planned to ship in a new version soon; installing libusb avoids the error.

message: CRITICAL:__main__:STLink error (20): DP wait
title: pyOCD: Intermittent 'STLink error (20): DP wait' on ST boards after power cycling
cause: After a power cycle the Mbed OS application starts and goes to sleep without the DBGMCU_CR debug-in-sleep bits set; pyOCD sets these bits only when it connects and cannot wake a target that is already sleeping.
fix: In debug builds keep the firmware from sleeping at all, or have it set the DBGMCU_CR bits (such as DBG_SLEEP) at startup. Connecting under reset (connect_mode=under-reset) allowed a connection, and updating the ST-Link firmware cleared the error on most of the boards.

message: Command "python setup.py egg_info" failed with error code 1
title: pyOCD: pip install pyocd 0.14.x fails in CI because of a non-UTF-8 locale
cause: setup.py read README.md with the default encoding, which was ASCII in the CI container, so a non-ASCII byte made decoding fail.
fix: Upgrade to pyOCD 0.15.0, which the maintainer said should fix it (#495), or declare a UTF-8 locale before calling pip.

message: DAP_TRANSFER response error
title: pyOCD: nRF52 flash over CMSIS-DAP on macOS fails with DAP_TRANSFER response error
cause: Command packets appear to get out of order, dropped or mixed up between pyOCD on macOS and a custom CMSIS-DAP firmware (private DAPLink fork on a K22F); the maintainer suspected the Ubuntu VM worked only because of lower USB performance.
fix: Add -Ocmsis_dap.limit_packets=1 (the =True form was not accepted until change #1259); the maintainer also suggested rebasing the firmware on the current DAPLink develop branch.

message: DeviceError: ... read thread exited
title: pyOCD: K64F via Raspberry Pi: 'read thread exited' errors during reset or flashing
cause: USB instability on the Raspberry Pi 3; the maintainer closed the issue as a Raspberry Pi USB problem.
fix: Suggestions, none confirmed: lower the DAP frequency, pass `--daparg limit_packets=True` (also needed under some VMs such as VirtualBox on Windows), or reset the target by sending a break over DAPLink's virtual COM port.

message: E Error while running debug sequence 'ResetSystem' (core M55_HP): __apid has invalid value (2097152)
title: pyOCD: Debug sequence fails with invalid __apid on Access Port v2 devices
cause: The AP address classes lacked apid handling for APv2.
fix: Use a pyOCD whose AP address classes handle apid, first in the standalone build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild3.

message: E Transfer error while reading AHB-AP#1 ROM table: Memory transfer fault @ 0xe00fefd0-0xe00fefff [ap]
title: pyOCD: CoreSight discovery fails on MEM-APs with SPROT field
cause: The HNONSEC bit in CSW was handled wrongly for MEM-APs that implement SPROT.
fix: Use a pyOCD with the MEM-AP CSW SPROT handling, first provided in the standalone pyOCD build v0.0.0-standalone-cbuild4.

message: ERRO download of "http://www.keil.com/pack/ARM.minar.pdsc" failed: unexpected end of file
title: pyOCD: pyocd pack -u fails to download the index or pack descriptors from keil.com
cause: The index and pack descriptor downloads failed because of a server-side problem at the pack host, not a pyOCD bug; some pdsc URLs returned HTML pages.
fix: Retry: the maintainers worked around it on the server and reported it fixed (a retest during the server change could still fail). Failures for a few vendors (e.g. Qorvo) are known and outside pyOCD's control.

message: ERRO download of "https://www.keil.com/pack/Keil.STM32G0xx_DFP.pdsc" failed: error trying to connect: unexpected end of file
title: pyOCD: pyocd pack install says 'No matching devices' because keil.com pack downloads fail
cause: The Rust Reqwest/RusTLS libraries used by cmsis-pack-manager could not download several pdsc files from the Keil server (unexpected end of file), so the index lacked the STM32 packs.
fix: Download the DFP from the Keil CMSIS-Pack list and pass it with --pack.

message: ERRO download of "https://www.keil.com/pack/Keil.STM32H7xx_DFP.pdsc" failed: unexpected end of file
title: pyOCD: STM32F7/H7/G0 packs not installable: pack download fails, 'No cores discovered'
cause: The STM32F7/H7/G0 pdsc downloads failed during the index update (the maintainer later says this is fixed; a separate problem is that cmsis-pack-manager parallelises the index download so much that Keil and NXP servers block it, cmsis-pack-manager#190). For 'No cores were discovered', STM32F7/H7 need DBGMCU writes to enable clocks, which packs do through debug sequences that pyOCD did not yet support.
fix: Download the DFP from the Keil pack list and pass it with --pack. The reporter also needed to update the ST-Link firmware and erase the flash before pyOCD connected reliably. Until debug sequences are supported, configure DBGMCU.CR in a pyOCD user script.

message: ERROR: Complete output from command python setup.py egg_info:
title: pyOCD: pip install pyocd fails in setup.py egg_info on Debian with bad marshal data
cause: The installed setuptools was older than 40, which pyOCD's setup.py requires (its setup_requires for setuptools >= 40.0 had no effect).
fix: Upgrade setuptools (e.g. pip install -U pip setuptools), then install pyOCD again; pip install --force-reinstall setuptools_scm_git_archive was suggested for a corrupt helper package.

message: ERROR:root:Too many page programming errors, aborting program operation
title: pyOCD: Flash programming errors 102 on FRDM-KL28Z because old DAPLink reports a clashing board ID
cause: The board's old DAPLink reported board ID 0290, which pyOCD maps to the FRDM-KW40Z (the KL28Z's ID had been changed to 0205), so pyOCD treated the board as a KW40Z.
fix: Update the DAPLink firmware (confirmed by the reporter), or force the target with `-t frdmkl28z`.

message: ERROR:root:eraseAll error: 104
title: pyOCD: eraseAll error 104 on a KL25Z chip erase
cause: Error 104 is the Kinetis SDK flash driver status for a protection violation: sectors are protected through the flash configuration field at 0x400, which blocks a chip erase.
fix: Run a mass erase: connect with pyocd-tool and run `unlock` (the unlock option of pyocd-flashtool was not implemented).

message: Entering into ISP mode failed: DPConnector.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'dp'
title: pyOCD: SPSDK breaks with pyOCD 0.35.0: DPConnector missing 'dp' argument
cause: pyOCD 0.35.0 changed the DPConnector constructor signature, breaking callers (such as NXP SPSDK) that passed only the probe.
fix: Pass the debug port explicitly as the second argument (DPConnector(probe, probe.session.board.target.dp)), as done on the SPSDK side; the maintainer said he would find a way to revert the API change.

message: Error: already open
title: pyOCD: Low-speed USB CMSIS-DAP v1 probe fails on Windows: packet size error then 'already open'
cause: On Windows the hidapi backend took the HID report size from the endpoint size (8 bytes for a low-speed device) instead of the 64 bytes in the HID report descriptor, so opening failed; the reporter suspected the failed open was not cleaned up, which gives 'already open' on the next attempt. On Linux pyOCD uses the PyUSB backend instead.
fix: Use a pyOCD version with change #1854 (hidapi backend revision), which the reporter confirmed works on Windows and macOS. Linux, which uses the PyUSB backend, remained broken in the thread.

message: Getting requirements to build wheel ... error
title: pyOCD: pip install from git develop fails in setuptools_scm with GPG signature
cause: setuptools_scm 6.4.2 fails on GPG-signed commits when git log shows signatures; the upstream fix (pypa/setuptools_scm#548) was due in 6.4.3, not yet released at the time.
fix: Disable signatures globally with 'git config --global log.showSignature false' before installing (setting it only in the repository did not help), or use setuptools_scm 6.4.3 once it is released.

message: ImportError: No module named pyocd.tools.gdb_server
title: pyOCD: ImportError for pyocd.tools.gdb_server after upgrading to 0.13
cause: pyOCD 0.13 renamed the package from pyOCD to pyocd; the maintainer suspected that on a case-insensitive filesystem an upgrade may leave the installed folder with the old name, so the import of pyocd fails. He could not reproduce it.
fix: Upgrade to the latest pyOCD with `pip install -U pyocd`, which resolved it for the reporter. Other suggestions in the thread: uninstall and reinstall in a virtualenv, or rename the installed package folder to pyocd by hand (needed by another user on Windows).

message: ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package
title: pyOCD: Building a standalone pyocd executable with PyInstaller fails
cause: Pointing PyInstaller at pyocd/tools/pyocd.py breaks its relative imports; later problems came from prettytable's pkg_resources distribution lookup and the SVD data zip not being bundled.
fix: Use the prebuilt binary distributions included in the pyOCD release assets instead of building your own.

message: MemoryError
title: pyOCD: MemoryError when reading a large memory block with 'savemem' on 32-bit Python
cause: A 32-bit Python process ran out of memory while building the buffer for a large savemem block read (pyOCD represents data as lists of integers).
fix: Use 64-bit Python; the reporter confirmed it works there.

message: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pyocd._version'
title: pyOCD: Running pyOCD tests from a source tree fails: No module named pyocd._version
cause: The pyocd._version module is missing when the tests run from a source tree in which pyOCD was not installed.
fix: Run `pip install -r dev-requirements.txt` in the repository root (not in a subfolder), which installs pyOCD in development mode; the reporter had first worked around it by adding a _version.py with version='0.18.0' by hand.

message: No ACK received
title: pyOCD: LPC55S28 flash fails with 'No ACK received'
cause: The target was not responding on SWD because the application had muxed one of the SWD pins to another function (the maintainer notes 'No ACK received' usually means low-power sleep or muxed SWD pins).
fix: Remove the application's pin configuration that reassigns the SWD pin; then flashing works.

message: No available boards are connected
title: pyOCD: pyocd lists no boards on Linux unless run with sudo
cause: On Linux a normal user lacked the access rights to the probe's USB device, so pyOCD found no boards while mbedls did; running with sudo worked.
fix: Run pyOCD with sudo; the reporter asked for documentation on how to run without sudo, and the issue was closed as a duplicate of #267.

message: No available boards are connected
title: pyOCD: pyocd does not list an nRF52 board that only has a J-Link firmware
cause: pyOCD at that time supported only the CMSIS-DAP protocol. A board whose interface runs J-Link firmware is invisible to it.
fix: Install the CMSIS-DAP interface firmware from Nordic on the board's interface MCU; pyOCD then sees the board.

message: No available debug probes are connected
title: pyOCD: WCH-Link CMSIS-DAP probe is not listed by pyocd on macOS
cause: pyOCD recognises HID CMSIS-DAP probes by 'CMSIS-DAP' in the product name; the WCH-Link's product string lacks it, hidapi does not report interface names, and the WCH-Link's HID interface string descriptor is broken, so the probe was ignored on macOS (Windows with pyocd 0.29.0 listed it).
fix: Install the maintainer's branch that also looks for 'CMSIS-DAP' in the hidapi device path (pip install -U git+https://github.com/flit/pyOCD@bugfix/hidapi_uid_and_if_name); the reporter confirmed the probe is then found.

message: No available debug probes are connected
title: pyOCD: WCH-Link CMSIS-DAP probe not detected
cause: pyOCD matches probes by product and interface name strings rather than VID/PID, and this WCH-Link (2a86:8011) is not fully USB compliant: it fails to answer string descriptor requests properly in some conditions.
fix: Matching by VID/PID pair was added on the develop branch (commit a926e94; PR #1399 discussed). Workaround on Linux: edit hidapi_backend.py to also accept 'WCH-Link' in the product name and run with PYOCD_USB_BACKEND=hidapiusb (with hidapi installed instead of hid).

message: No connected debug probes
title: pyOCD: Executable built with PyInstaller reports 'No connected debug probes'
cause: PyInstaller does not collect pyOCD's probe and RTOS plug-ins (package entry points) and package data by default, so the built executable finds no probe.
fix: Collect the 'pyocd.probe' and 'pyocd.rtos' entry points and add the pyocd and pylink package folders as data in the .spec file. On another PC the ST-Link driver may also be needed. Releases from v0.38.0 include prebuilt binaries.

message: No emulator with serial number <SN> found.
title: pyOCD: J-Link open by serial number fails with 'No emulator with serial number found'
cause: With jlink.non_interactive enabled (default), pyOCD disables dialog boxes in the J-Link DLL before opening the probe, which made opening by serial number fail with J-Link DLL 9.24.01.
fix: Set 'jlink.non_interactive: false' in pyocd.yaml as a workaround, or use a pyOCD version with the fix from change #1927.

message: PC register is not available
title: pyOCD: Picoprobe unreliable with pyocd (PC register not available)
cause: Probable signal-integrity trouble; the picoprobe code speeds up SWD by assuming positive acknowledgements from the target, and the firmware leaves the pins at a fast slew rate.
fix: Lower the SWD clock (-f 400000) and replug the probe when problems show; -Opicoprobe.safeswd=True disables the assumed acknowledgements (much slower).

title: pyOCD: CMSIS-DAP v1 probe 'not found' on Windows/macOS after upgrading from 0.36 to 0.40
cause: After upgrading from 0.36.0 to 0.40.0, opening a CMSIS-DAP v1 probe through the hidapi backend on Windows failed with 'Probe ... not found' although pyocd list showed it; the thread does not state the root cause.
fix: Use a pyOCD version containing change #1854 (hidapi backend changes), which the reporter confirmed works on Windows.

message: Probe NKBA2RU557ZLCOPTYPWHIX3IZUQ5ZH7B not found [__main__]
title: pyOCD: CMSIS-DAP v2 probe without USB serial number is listed but 'not found' when opening
cause: pyocd list shows a generated unique ID for a CMSIS-DAP v2 probe that has no USB serial number, but opening the probe by that ID fails with 'not found'. The reporter suspected the lookup by the generated ID when the probe is opened; the thread gives no confirmed root cause.
fix: Use a pyOCD version containing the fix for serial-less CMSIS-DAP v2 probes (change #2007), which the reporter confirmed.

message: Reply contains invalid hex digit 120
title: pyOCD: gdb drops pyocd gdbserver connection: 'Reply contains invalid hex digit 120'
cause: The core was not halted when gdb connected (here a watchdog reset the target after pyocd halted it). Register reads then fail and pyocd returns 'xxxxxxxx' as unavailable values in the first stop reply, which gdb cannot parse as hex.
fix: Make sure the core is halted when gdb attaches: disable the watchdog, or configure it to stop while debugging.

message: Target type stm32h745zihx not recognized. Use 'pyocd list --targets' to see currently available target types.
title: pyOCD: Board ID maps to a target name pyOCD does not recognise (stm32h745zihx)
cause: The board ID table appears to assign a wrong target name (stm32h745zihx) to the DISCO-H745I board.
fix: Pass the right target explicitly, e.g. -t STM32H745XIHx. Flash loading then still failed (flash algorithm not halted, IPSR=3) and the thread leaves that open.

message: TransferError
title: pyOCD: pyocd-gdbserver TransferError right after 'DAP SWD MODE initialized' on an LPC812 board
cause: pyOCD could not even read the DP IDCODE register, which is always readable while the SW-DP is powered and its pins are connected, so the maintainer judged it a hardware problem rather than a pyOCD one.
fix: Check the SWD connection and the target's power before suspecting pyOCD.

message: TransferError: No ACK received
title: pyOCD: PSoC6: gdb 'monitor reset' fails with TransferError and kills the connection
cause: After a reset PSoC6 drops back to JTAG mode and loses DAP state, so the DAP must be fully re-initialised; since 0.28.0 dp.init() goes through the shared probe proxy, which increments its connect count and then turns the SWJ switch sequence into a no-op.
fix: Pull request #1018 is meant to fix reconnecting; the maintainer asked the reporter to verify it. The reporter's tested workaround in the PSoC6 target code re-initialises the DAP after reset (SWJ sequence, reset_did_occur on the APs, read DP IDR, clear sticky errors, power up debug).

message: Unable to read memory
title: pyOCD: Cannot read memory at peripheral register addresses with pyOCD
cause: pyOCD failed to read memory-mapped peripheral registers that the J-Link GDB server could read; the reporter suspected unmet memory-map requirements, and the thread does not confirm a cause.
fix: Use patch release 0.1.1 or later, whose pyOCD fixes these reads. The GDB command 'set mem inaccessible-by-default off' was only discussed as an additional option.

message: Unhandled exception in handle_message: string argument without an encoding
title: pyOCD: Semihosting output over gdbserver raises TypeError 'string argument without an encoding'
cause: A string/bytes conversion bug in SemihostAgent._get_string() (six.ensure_str(bytes(bytearray(''))...)) raises TypeError for semihosting write requests under Python 3.
fix: Fixed by the maintainer's commit, which the reporter confirmed works. Before that, replacing the failing line in _get_string() with target_str = "" removed the error.

message: Unhandled exception in handle_message: type object 'Target' has no attribute 'CATCH_CORE_RESET'
title: pyOCD: Flashing via gdb fails: type object 'Target' has no attribute 'CATCH_CORE_RESET'
cause: Regression after CATCH_CORE_RESET was renamed: the LPC1768 built-in target's set_reset_catch still used the old name, so reset-and-halt during flashing raised AttributeError.
fix: Fixed by PR #821, merged to master; use a pyOCD version that includes it.

message: Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Console key values must be between 0 and 255 inclusive. (Parameter 'key')
title: pyOCD: PowerShell window closes after pyocd list, flash or reset on Windows
cause: PowerShell itself crashes: its console key reader (PSConsoleReadLine.ReadKey) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException a moment after commands such as pyocd list, json or reset return. Seen with Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.2, not with cmd.exe.
fix: Run pyocd from cmd.exe (this also works inside a PowerShell window). pyocd --version and the interactive pyocd commander do not trigger it.

message: UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xa6 in position 6075: illegal multibyte sequence
title: pyOCD: pip install pyocd fails on Windows with a gbk UnicodeDecodeError in setup.py
cause: On a system whose default code page is gbk, setup.py opened README.md, which contains non-ASCII characters, without specifying an encoding.
fix: Use a pyOCD version that contains PR #495, which fixed reading the file in setup.py.

message: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '01B6'
title: pyOCD: CMSIS-DAP probe open fails with ValueError parsing the firmware version string
cause: Some probe firmwares (Microchip EDBG, Particle DAPLink) put a vendor firmware revision in the DAP_Info field that pre-2.1 CMSIS-DAP specs loosely called firmware version but that means protocol version; pyOCD tried to parse it as numbers.
fix: Upgrade to pyOCD 0.32.0 or later, where the maintainer says this is resolved (the change discussed was to handle the parse error and default to CMSIS-DAP protocol 1.0.0 for unknown values).

message: W Failed to add data chunk: no memory region defined for address 0x00008000 [file_programmer]
title: pyOCD: HC32L130 built-in target cannot write above 32 KB
cause: The built-in memory map for the part covered only the first 32 KB of flash.
fix: Use the vendor pack with the specific part name (--pack HDSC.HC32L130.1.0.1.pack --target hc32l130f8ua), which flashes and runs. PR #1590 seemed to fix the built-in target; this was not confirmed.

message: W No matching devices. Please make sure the pack index is up to date. [pack_cmd]
title: pyOCD: pyocd pack find or install returns nothing after pack update
cause: The maintainer suggested that cmsis-pack-manager 0.5.1 can fail pdsc downloads because too many are started concurrently, leaving the index incomplete; this might explain the reports, but nobody confirmed it.
fix: Update cmsis-pack-manager to 0.5.2 (pip install -U cmsis-pack-manager), which addresses the concurrent-download failures, and run pyocd pack update again.

message: W Timed out waiting for core to halt after reset (state is RUNNING) [cortex_m]
title: pyOCD: target was not halted as expected after calling flash algorithm routine since pyOCD 0.36
cause: Starting with the 0.36 series, flashing or chip erase on several targets (HK32F030M, STM32L071, a Nuvoton M0A23, NXP FRDM-MCXN947) fails with 'target was not halted as expected after calling flash algorithm routine (IPSR=3)', while 0.35.1 works on the same hardware. One user saw it intermittently, together with a timeout waiting for the core to halt after reset, and suspected the halt-after-reset sequence. The thread has no root cause; it is still seen with 0.41 and 0.44.1.
fix: Install pyOCD 0.35.1 (pip install pyocd==0.35.1), which works on the same hardware. For NXP MCX boards under Zephyr, west flash -r linkserver avoids the problem. Tuning connect mode and reset timing did not make the failure go away reliably.

message: WARNING:__main__:No matching devices. Please make sure the pack index is up to date.
title: pyOCD: pyocd pack --install stm32g071rb: 'No matching devices' after failed index downloads
cause: cmsis-pack-manager could not fetch the STM32 pdsc files from keil.com (a problem deep in RustLS; curl downloads them fine), so the device was not in the local index.
fix: Download the DFP from the Keil CMSIS-Pack list and pass it to pyOCD with --pack. One user still got 'Target type not recognized' with --pack and with a pack: entry in the config file; that stayed open in the thread.

message: Waiting for a debug probe to be connected...
title: pyOCD: Debug start on Windows hangs with 'Waiting for a debug probe to be connected...'
cause: On Windows pyOCD found no libusb library, so STLink and CMSIS-DAP v2 probes were unsupported and the server kept waiting for a probe; 'pip install libusb' did not provide the DLL.
fix: Download libusb from libusb.info and place its DLL next to python.exe, matching the 32- or 64-bit architecture of the Python installation (maintainer's advice, not confirmed in the thread).

message: flash init timed out
title: pyOCD: Flash load after halting a running target fails with IPSR=3 or flash init timeout
cause: Flash algorithms typically assume the device has been reset before they run; loading after only halting a running application is not supported, and the algorithm then faults or times out.
fix: Reset the target and halt it before programming: use 'reset halt' in the commander, or 'monitor reset halt' before 'load' in gdb. 'pyocd flash' already does this by default.

message: mbedgt: No module named pyOCD.board
title: pyOCD: mbedgt fails with 'No module named pyOCD.board' after upgrading pyOCD to 0.13 or newer
cause: htrun (mbed-host-tests, used by greentea) was not compatible with pyOCD 0.13 and later and still looked for the pyOCD.board module.
fix: Upgrade mbed-host-tests to 1.4.4 or newer (upgrading mbed-greentea also brings a newer one); downgrading pyOCD to 0.12 also avoided the error.

message: pylink.errors.JLinkException: No emulator with serial number 1064xxxxx2 found.
title: pyOCD: J-Link fails to open with 'No emulator with serial number' on newer J-Link DLLs
cause: A known issue between pylink and J-Link DLL versions 9.14 and above: opening the probe by serial number fails at random. One user suspected several pylink.JLink instances alive at once; the maintainer saw them destroyed as expected.
fix: Use a pyOCD build containing change #1927 (the issue was closed as resolved without a test report). On Windows some dialog boxes may then appear.

message: pyocd-flashtool: error: argument -t/--target: invalid choice: 'stm32l476rg'
title: pyOCD: Target from a downloaded CMSIS-Pack not found: --pack must be given on every pyocd command
cause: The pack was only supplied to the gdbserver invocation; --pack does not install the pack, so every pyOCD tool invocation needs it.
fix: Pass --pack <file> to every pyOCD invocation, or list the packs once under pack: in a pyocd.yaml in the working directory (or pass --config); with that, pyocd flash found the target.

message: pyocd-gdbserver: error: invalid target option 'efm32g890f128'
title: pyOCD: pyocd-gdbserver rejects pack-defined targets with 'invalid target option'
cause: The deprecated pyocd-gdbserver tool validates the --target name against built-in targets only (validate_target() in pyocd/tools/gdb_server.py), so pack targets are rejected, while the new `pyocd gdbserver` accepts them.
fix: Launch `pyocd gdbserver --pack <file> -t <target>` instead of pyocd-gdbserver (for example in an IDE debug configuration such as cortex-debug).

message: uncaught exception: 'CY8C6xx7' object has no attribute 'options'
title: pyOCD: gdbserver for PSoC6 (cy8c6xxa, cy8c6xx7) crashes: object has no attribute 'options'
cause: Regression after 0.16.1 in the PSoC6 target classes (CY8C6xxA, CY8C6xx7): core creation passes the target object where Target.__init__ expects the session, so reading session.options fails.
fix: Upgrade to pyOCD 0.22.0 or later.

message: uncaught exception: 'CY8C6xxA' object has no attribute 'options'
title: pyOCD: Flashing PSoC6 fails with "'CY8C6xxA' object has no attribute 'options'"
cause: Bug in the PSoC6 (CY8C6xxA) target class in 0.21.0, a duplicate of #680.
fix: Fixed on master; use a pyOCD version after 0.21.0 that includes the fix.

message: uncaught exception: 'MemoryMap' object has no attribute 'get_region_by_name'
title: pyOCD: flash script fails: 'MemoryMap' object has no attribute 'get_region_by_name'
cause: get_region_by_name() was removed from MemoryMap after 0.24 in favour of a general lookup; the user-script example still used the old name.
fix: Use target.memory_map.get_first_matching_region(name="flexspi") (keyword arguments match any region attribute); the documentation example was fixed in #849.

message: uncaught exception: 'module' object has no attribute 'BadZipFile'
title: pyOCD: pyocd list --targets fails with BadZipFile after a broken pack index download
cause: cmsis-pack-manager constructed a wrong download URL for packs whose URL lacked a trailing slash (ARMmbed/cmsis-pack-manager#95), so the downloaded pack was garbage and reading it ended in the BadZipFile AttributeError, which the maintainer still had to investigate.
fix: Update cmsis-pack-manager once the release with the fix is out; pyocd pack --clean removes the error but also the pack. Meanwhile download the pack manually and pass it with --pack (e.g. pyocd gdbserver --pack <file>) or list it under pack: in pyocd.yaml.

message: uncaught exception: The device has no langid
title: pyOCD: 'The device has no langid' on Linux is an USB permission problem
cause: pyusb catches the error when reading the langids and stores an empty tuple, then raises ValueError. The real cause is missing access rights to the USB device ([Errno 13] Access denied).
fix: Run pyocd-gdbserver as root (sudo); the issue was closed because PR #262 addresses it, without a release named.

message: uncaught exception: Unable to open device
title: pyOCD: hidapi 'Unable to open device' on macOS with system Python
cause: With the Python shipped by macOS the HID device path came back empty, so the CMSIS-DAP interface could not be opened.
fix: Use a Python installed with Homebrew instead of the macOS system Python, and install pyOCD into it.

message: uncaught exception: local variable 'file_obj' referenced before assignment
title: pyOCD: pyocd flash with a nonexistent file raises UnboundLocalError instead of a clear message
cause: The image file passed to pyocd flash does not exist, and the loader's error path then closes a file object that was never assigned; a proper error also needs the ArgumentError class that PR #587 adds.
fix: Check that the image path exists. The misleading exception was to be fixed once PR #587 is merged; no release is named.

message: uncaught exception: name 'flashPtr' is not defined
title: pyOCD: pyocd cmd W32 to a flash address fails with NameError flashPtr
cause: program_phrase() in pyOCD's flash code tested an undefined variable flashPtr in its alignment check instead of the address, so a W32 to a flash address raised NameError.
fix: The maintainers took the bug on; the reporter's correction is to check address % min_len in program_phrase(). Use a pyOCD version that carries the correction.

message: uncaught exception: name 'os' is not defined
title: pyOCD: pyocd commander --elf crashes with 'name os is not defined'
cause: Regression in commands/commander.py: the os module is not imported and self.target.elf should be self.session.target.elf, so --elf crashes.
fix: Apply the reporter's patch (import os, use self.session.target.elf); the maintainer said he would ship a fix with it shortly.

message: uncaught exception: unbound method _pack_target__init__() must be called with _PackTargetMethods instance as first argument (got Session instance instead)
title: pyOCD: Loading an STM32F401RE pack under Python 2.7 crashes with unbound method error
